[![Required](https://github.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/777genius/universal-agent-plugins) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/universal-agent-plugins?label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/universal-agent-plugins) [![Agent Plugins 1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent%20Plugins-1.0.0-7257FF)](https://agent-plugins.org/specification) [![Agent Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agent%20Skills-standard-7257FF)](https://agentskills.io/specification) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [Documentation](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/) · [Browse plugins](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/plugins/) · [Build a plugin](#build-plugins)

Install and manage plugins and Skills across your AI agents with one CLI. Share `uap.toml` (package list) and `uap.lock` (exact versions) to restore your setup on another computer or with your team. **More than a one-time installer:** UAP combines a [searchable plugin directory](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/plugins/), independent [Agent Skills](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/agent-skills/), native multi-agent installation, managed repair/removal, portable dependency locks, and [Go/TypeScript SDKs](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/sdk/). Review [product capabilities and release boundaries](docs/PRODUCT_CAPABILITIES.md) for evidence and limitations.

## Contents - [Use plugins](#use-plugins) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Install the CLI](#install-the-cli) - [What the CLI does](#what-the-cli-does) - [More capabilities](#more-capabilities) - [Install for one project](#install-for-one-project) - [Restore your plugin setup](#restore-your-plugin-setup) - [Install from other sources](#install-from-other-sources) - [Supported clients](#supported-clients) - [More commands](#more-commands) - [Find and verify plugins](#find-and-verify-plugins) - [Safe updates and removal](#safe-updates-and-removal) - [SDKs and integrations](#sdks-and-integrations) - [Build plugins](#build-plugins) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) **Build plugins:** [authoring guide](website/source/en/build/index.md) · [package layout](website/source/en/build/layout.md) · [validate package](website/source/en/build/checks.md). Source-built `agentplugins author` supports scaffolding and diagnostics, but **native CLI 0.1.110 does not ship it yet**. Standard-first bundle export and marketplace publication are not part of the current `author` command. ## Use plugins ### Quick start Install a [supported agent](#supported-clients) first. Then, with Node.js 22+, add Context7: ```bash npx universal-agent-plugins add context7 ``` Choose from the detected agents, follow any sign-in or approval steps, then start a new session. This installs for your user account. To keep plugins in one repository, use [project installation](#install-for-one-project). **Choose your agents** **Review the installation plan — Playwright example** **Follow installation progress — Playwright example** ### Install the CLI Choose one method. Only npm requires Node.js; Homebrew and the native scripts do not. **macOS and Linux — Homebrew:** ```bash brew install 777genius/agentplugins/agentplugins agentplugins add context7 ``` **macOS and Linux — native installer:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/main/install.sh | sh -s -- add context7 ``` **Windows — PowerShell:** ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/main/install.ps1 | iex & "$HOME\.local\bin\agentplugins.exe" add context7 ``` **npm — Node.js 22+:** ```bash npm install -g universal-agent-plugins agentplugins add context7 ``` The native scripts verify the download's checksum and version, then install to `$HOME/.local/bin`. Add that directory to `PATH` to use `agentplugins` by name. Plugins may need additional runtimes; see [installation help](docs/NATIVE_INSTALL.md). For the latest stable native installer, see [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/releases/latest). Check `agentplugins version`: npm and Homebrew can lag behind native releases. Code in `main` may not be released yet. ## What the CLI does - Installs supported package components in one or more agents. - Records exact versions for repeatable installs. - Updates, repairs, and removes managed files without overwriting unrelated content. - Reports any remaining approval, sign-in, or reload steps. ## More capabilities For AI-agent / headless installation, see the [agent-first CLI guide](docs/AGENT_CLI.md): explicit targets and scope, read-only Skills discovery, JSON results, and lifecycle verification. New source-only commands are labelled separately from released CLI behavior. | Need | How UAP helps | | --- | --- | | Multiple agents | `add --target codex,claude` with separate outcomes and any remaining activation steps. | | Standalone Skills | `skills add` with a browser picker or explicit `--skill` selections; see [Skills installation](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/use/install.html#install-agent-skills). | | Sources outside the registry | Reviewed local package directories, Git/SSH sources and complete ZIP/TAR archives; see [source formats](docs/DIRECT_PACKAGE_SOURCES.md). | | Team/project reproducibility | Commit `uap.toml` and `uap.lock`, then run `install --locked --scope project`; see [dependency environments](docs/UAP_DEPENDENCIES.md). | | Package creation and checks | [Authoring guide](website/source/en/build/index.md) for source-build templates, validation and compatibility checks (not in 0.1.110 native CLI). | | Development-only roots | `[dev-dependencies]` in `uap.toml` with explicit targets, omitted from consumers; requires a release containing this feature. | | Moving a user setup | `deps export` and `deps import --install`; no credentials or live data are exported. | | Maintenance | `doctor`, `outdated`, `update --dry-run`, `repair --dry-run`, explicit remove and scope flags. | | Application integration | [Go Installer](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/sdk/go-installer.html) or [TypeScript Management SDK](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/sdk/typescript-management.html). | | Typed agent callbacks | [Go Hooks SDK](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/sdk/go-hooks.html), with event- and release-specific support. | File preparation, native activation, MCP execution and authentication are separate checkpoints. Check each target's result after a multi-agent operation. ## Install for one project Use `--scope project` (CLI 0.1.93+) to install in one repository without changing your user setup. **Signed Directory short names** Merged installer PR #725 supports explicit Project placement for an eligible signed package and its required dependencies, using each selected client's real Project capabilities. Historical User runtime evidence is not Project activation evidence. In the published stable CLI: ```sh cd /path/to/project agentplugins add context7 --target codex --scope project --dry-run ``` Review the plan before omitting `--dry-run`. Unsupported clients or mandatory components fail closed; there is no implicit User fallback. **Alternative: exact Git source.** For reproducibility, copy a compatible, commit-pinned Git source from the [catalog](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/plugins/) and replace the placeholders: ```sh cd /path/to/project agentplugins add github:OWNER/REPOSITORY@FULL_COMMIT_SHA//PACKAGE_PATH \ --scope project --target codex ``` Use a full 40-character commit SHA; omit `//PACKAGE_PATH` for a root package. Direct Git is an alternative to a signed Directory alias. Neither route bypasses native client trust or complete dependency authorization. **Share and restore** Commit the generated `uap.toml` and `uap.lock`; add `.uap/` to `.gitignore`. In another checkout, install UAP and the required agents, then run from the project root: ```sh agentplugins install --locked --scope project ``` `--locked` requires a lockfile matching the manifest and restores its exact versions. **Add standalone Skills** ```sh agentplugins skills add owner/repository --ui --scope project ``` Use a real Skills repository; `--ui` opens a browser picker. Outside the project, add `--project-root /path/to/project`. Always include `--scope project` with add, update, repair, and remove. Otherwise, they use your user setup—even inside the project. ChatGPT has no native project installation. See the [project guide](docs/PROJECT_INSTALLATION.md) for maintenance and the [project support table](docs/PROJECT_CLIENT_SUPPORT.md) for each agent's limits. ## Restore your plugin setup Export your saved user-wide setup to an empty folder: ```sh agentplugins deps export /path/to/transfer ``` Copy `uap.toml` and `uap.lock` to the new computer, install UAP and the required agents, then import from the folder containing those files: ```sh agentplugins deps import /path/to/transfer --install ``` Only `uap.toml` and `uap.lock` travel. These commands use your user setup, not a project's. Sign-ins, secrets, agent settings, and plugin data need separate setup or backup. Packages must remain available from their sources or the destination cache; this is not an offline backup. Check supported agents with `agentplugins deps status`. [Dependency guide](docs/UAP_DEPENDENCIES.md) · [Import and recovery](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/use/manage.html#restore-on-another-machine) ## Install from other sources Install an Agent Plugins 1.0 package from a local folder, Git (HTTPS or SSH), or a ZIP/TAR/TAR.GZ archive (local or HTTPS). No catalog entry is required. Only `plugin.json` is supported as the package manifest: | File or folder | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `plugin.json` | Required package manifest | | `skills/` | Optional reusable instructions | | `mcp.json` | Optional MCP servers | | `hooks/` | Optional client-specific extensions | Skills are instructions; MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers connect agents to tools. Both work across supported clients; hooks depend on the client. See [source formats and credentials](docs/DIRECT_PACKAGE_SOURCES.md). Standalone `SKILL.md` files use `agentplugins skills add`, not `agentplugins add`. It accepts GitHub repositories and HTTPS publishers with a Skills index. Publisher installs need an exact `--skill` name; see the [Skills guide](docs/AGENT_SKILLS_INSTALLER.md). ## Supported clients **User** installs into your agent profile; **Project** installs into one selected workspace. Agents may still ask you to trust the project, sign in, or restart. | Agent | User scope | Project scope | Setup | What you do after installing | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Claude Code** | Plugins, Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Trust the workspace and reload Claude Code if prompted. | | **Codex CLI** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Open a new session; approve project MCP access if prompted. | | **OpenCode** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Start a new session and review effective project settings. | | **Cursor** | Plugins, Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Prepared | Reload Cursor; enable plugins or MCP servers if requested. | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | Plugins, Skills, MCP | Plugins, Skills, MCP (prepared) | Automatic | Restart Copilot CLI if requested. | | **Gemini CLI** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Reload Gemini CLI and approve tool access if prompted. | | **Qoder** | Plugins, Skills, MCP, hooks | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Restart Qoder and review MCP permissions. | | **Pi** | Extensions, Skills, MCP | Extensions, Skills, MCP | Automatic | Trust the project and reload Pi resources. | | **Windsurf / Devin** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Open or restart Devin in the selected project; review access. | | **Kimi Code** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Automatic | Run /reload or /new and review MCP permissions. | | **Cline** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP (prepared) | Automatic | Select the project MCP settings path and reload Cline. | | **Kiro** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP | Guided | The CLI configures supported Skills and MCP automatically; sign in, approve access, and restart if prompted. | | **Grok Build** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP (prepared) | Automatic | Open the selected project in Grok, review trust, and follow any remaining enablement or reload steps; verify Skills and MCP. | | **Hermes Agent** | Skills, MCP | Skills, MCP (prepared) | Automatic | Restart Hermes and trust the project; Project MCP requires a verified standalone Hermes bundle and an explicitly confirmed UAP project session. | | **Google Antigravity** | Plugins, Skills, MCP | Plugins, Skills, MCP | Prepared | Open or reload Antigravity; review trust and verify the prepared plugin is discovered and enabled in the selected scope. | | **ChatGPT** | Desktop local plugins; Web connected apps | Not supported | Guided | Desktop: local install via Codex CLI; Web: connect or install in ChatGPT. | **Setup terms:** Automatic = UAP installs supported components; Guided = follow client prompts; Prepared = files are ready but need activation; Manual = complete setup in the app. After confirmation, UAP completes supported native setup and reports remaining trust, sign-in or reload steps. This matrix describes the released installer capabilities of [native CLI 0.1.115](https://github.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/releases/tag/agentplugins-v0.1.115) for every agent above; signed Directory packages still need an eligible target. Installation does not prove native runtime activation or vendor authentication. See the [compatibility reference](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/reference/client-compatibility.html) for tested versions, platforms, and setup steps.
Client-specific setup and limits Since CLI 0.1.102, the published CLI supports Pi [native extensions](docs/PI_NATIVE_EXTENSION_CONTRACT.md), Skills and stdio/Streamable HTTP MCP in user and eligible project scope. Each signed Directory release still needs an explicit Pi target; direct pinned Git sources use a separate CLI-validated installation path. For scoped trust, activation and native E2E limits, see the [project compatibility matrix](docs/PROJECT_CLIENT_SUPPORT.md). Hermes supports User Skills and stdio/Streamable HTTP MCP, plus Project Skills at the selected Git root. Project MCP is prepared only with a verified standalone Hermes host bundle and an explicitly confirmed UAP project session; ordinary startup does not select it. A Hermes host installed from source supports User MCP or Project Skills only; this does not restrict plugin Git sources. Antigravity prepares owned User/Project native plugins with Skills and supported MCP; verify discovery, trust and enablement in the IDE. Preparation does not prove IDE activation. For both clients, ordinary portable commands project to Skills; explicit-only commands are withheld because these hosts cannot enforce explicit invocation. Grok Build, Kimi Code, and Qoder support stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP in user scope. Grok Project plugin enablement is opt-in on Linux with Grok 1.0.70 and preserves an existing disabled preference. Devin User and Project delivery require 3000.11.205 or 3000.12.57. For GitHub Copilot CLI stable 1.0.81 or later, or prerelease 1.0.81-N with N of 8 or higher, UAP registers a compatible Agent Plugins 1.0 package as a native project plugin in `.github/copilot/settings.local.json`. It keeps loose project Skills and MCP for new installs on an older or unobserved version, packages with commands, an app, invalid components, bundled stdio executables or `PLUGIN_DATA` launchers, and existing loose installations. UAP reports the registration as Prepared; start a new Copilot CLI session to load it. Cline Project MCP requires an explicitly selected managed session/settings path. Qoder also preserves native hooks, commands, and bundled binaries. See [portable commands](docs/UAP_COMMANDS.md) for command delivery and limits. For guided Context7 setup in ChatGPT and Kiro: ```bash npx universal-agent-plugins add context7 --target chatgptweb,kiro --no-save ``` ChatGPT requires Developer Mode and custom apps. You must install the prepared package yourself and select it in a new chat. This command uses `--no-save` because ChatGPT setup cannot be saved as a portable dependency. To save plugins for other agents, install those separately without `--no-save`. See the [Context7 setup guide](docs/CONTEXT7_CHATGPT_KIRO_E2E.md). Codex supports stdio and Streamable HTTP MCP, but excludes SSE components; see [transport details](docs/CODEX_TRANSPORT_EVIDENCE.md).
## More commands Omit `--target` to choose agents interactively; name them explicitly in scripts. ```bash # Find and inspect packages agentplugins search docs agentplugins info context7 # Install in specific agents agentplugins add context7 --target codex,claude # Maintain an installed plugin agentplugins update context7 --target codex,claude agentplugins repair context7 --target codex,claude agentplugins remove context7 --target codex,claude agentplugins outdated --all agentplugins update --all agentplugins doctor # Validate and try a local package agentplugins validate ./my-plugin agentplugins add ./my-plugin ``` Local folder installs are not saved as portable dependencies. Use a pinned Git or HTTPS archive source to restore the package on another computer. ## Find and verify plugins [Browse the catalog](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/plugins/) or run `agentplugins search`. Reviewed and unreviewed results are labelled separately. Discovery is not an endorsement; packages are checked again before installation. To list a package, see [registry contributions](https://github.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins-registry/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Safe updates and removal Use `--dry-run` to preview changes without modifying managed client files. Security checks may still download scanners or metadata. No install telemetry is sent. UAP checks packages, clients, and file ownership before making changes. It preserves unrelated content and external edits, reports conflicts, and rolls back failures only where safe. Check every agent's result after a multi-agent operation: some may succeed while others need attention. Repair restores managed files. Sign-in and testing inside the agent remain separate. [Removal and retained data](docs/REMOVAL_SAFETY.md) · [Steps requiring your approval](docs/INSTALLER_AUTOMATION_PRINCIPLE.md) UAP is an independent community project, unaffiliated with OpenAI, Agent Plugins, or the client vendors. ## SDKs and integrations For Go Hooks, host detection, installation, and TypeScript management, see the [SDK integration guides](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/sdk/).
Agent Notifications
Desktop notifications, sounds, and click-to-focus for AI coding agents.
Use the [Go SDK](sdk/README.md) for typed agent hooks and [Go installer components](install/integrationctl/agentplugins/installer/README.md) to embed plugin management in your app. The [TypeScript SDK](sdks/typescript/README.md), `universal-agent-plugins-management-sdk`, calls the CLI's local management API. Pin compatible SDK and CLI versions separately; see the [management guide](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/use/manage.html#local-management-api). ## Build plugins Create a package directory with root `plugin.json`, with optional `skills/` and `mcp.json`. `plugin.json` is the only supported authoring manifest. Validate and install it with the [local-package commands](#more-commands). The [Build guide](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/build/) covers Skills and MCP packages; start with the [Use / Build quickstart](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/guide/quickstart.html).
Authoring commands (qualified authoring or source build required) The current npm and native installer releases do not include `agentplugins author`. In qualified authoring builds, `agentplugins author` is the public authoring entrypoint. For example: ```bash agentplugins author init ./my-plugin --template skill --name my-plugin agentplugins author validate ./my-plugin agentplugins author inspect ./my-plugin agentplugins author test ./my-plugin ``` In qualified/source builds, MCP execution is available through `author test` and `author dev`. Dependency bootstrap apply currently requires Linux; dry-run planning can be used on other platforms. Local stdio development requires Linux, successful process-containment and bubblewrap preflights, and a supported system Node path. See the [stdio guide](https://universal-agent-plugins.com/docs/en/build/mcp-stdio.html). Client projection, export/bundle, and publication are not exposed by the current authoring CLI. Native installer [releases](https://github.com/777genius/universal-agent-plugins/releases) use `agentplugins-v*` tags; they do not include these authoring commands.
## Contributing See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the development workflow. Run: ```bash go test ./... make vet ``` [Security policy](SECURITY.md) · [Support boundary](docs/SUPPORT.md) · [Client E2E evidence](docs/AGENTPLUGINS_CLIENT_E2E.md) ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Third-party components retain their original licenses; see [NOTICE](NOTICE).

repository.description: An open-source, plugin-driven AHP server with native Claude and pi agents, ACP agents (Codex, Copilot, Gemini), model proxying, tools and MCP servers, sandboxed computers and terminals, automations, conversational bots, and a web UI (ahpw). Users, permissions and usage tracking are built in. Build your own host and plugins with @ahpd/sdk.

repository.readme:
# ahpd - agent host platform [![CI](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![@ahpd/server](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fserver?label=%40ahpd%2Fserver)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/server) [![@ahpd/sdk](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fsdk?label=%40ahpd%2Fsdk)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/sdk) [![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-ahpio.github.io%2Fahpd-0b7285)](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/) ![license MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![node >=22](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22-5fa04e) ![Agent Host Protocol 1.1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/AHP-1.1.0-0b7285) ![runs on Node, Bun, Deno](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20on-Node%20%7C%20Bun%20%7C%20Deno-495057) **Run your AI agents anywhere. Control them from anywhere.** `ahpd` is an open-source, self-hosted platform that brings multiple AI agents together. Run Claude Code SDK, Pi SDK, ACP agents (Codex, Copilot, Gemini, and more), or your own custom harness using supported subscriptions or API keys. Extend their capabilities with plugins, tools, connectors, MCP servers, and integrations. Schedule tasks or run sessions on your computer, remote servers, or in containers, with full control over your environments and resources. Whether it's for personal use or an organization, manage access, monitor usage, and control budgets from one place. Connect from your browser, desktop, terminal, or phone. Your sessions and work stay in sync across every client. > It also has a `shared editing` feature for real-time collaboration. > > **And this is just the beginning.** ahpd is an extensible platform, built to grow with new agents, integrations, and possibilities. [Read the documentation](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/) · [GitHub](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/NWvnuqEQxG) [ahpio.com](https://ahpio.com)

--- ## Start in minutes Install with one line on Linux or macOS: ```bash curl -fsSL https://ahpio.com/ahpd/install.sh | bash ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://ahpio.com/ahpd/install.ps1 | iex ``` The script checks for Node 22.18 or newer, installs `@ahpd/server` without sudo, adds `ahpd` to your PATH, and runs `ahpd configure`. [Install options](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/INSTALL) Or install with npm, then run the setup: ```bash npm install -g @ahpd/server --allow-scripts=node-pty ahpd configure ``` Choose your agents, network settings, and project folders. To add an agent later, run `ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-claude`. Start the host: ```bash ahpd start --path /work/project ``` Your host is ready for an AHP client. Connect from the terminal with ahpc: ```bash npx @softov/ahpc --host ws://127.0.0.1:9187 ``` ### 🗂️ Serve multiple projects ```bash ahpd --path /work/api --path /work/web ``` Project paths are catalogue entries, **not filesystem sandboxes**. Access to other paths depends on the configured host capabilities and permissions. ### 🔐 Connect remotely By default, the host listens on loopback. To listen on another interface, configure a connection token: ```bash ahpd --host 0.0.0.0 --connection-token-file ~/.config/ahpd/token ``` Only expose the host to networks you trust, and protect the token. See the [remote access documentation](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/REMOTE). --- ## Your agents. Your machines. Your control. Run the agents you prefer, manage how they work, and stay in control of your infrastructure, access, and spending. AI agents can help you write code, fix problems, manage files, and automate tasks. But they often depend on the terminal or application where you started them. ahpd gives your agents a place to run and gives you a way to reach them. **⏳ [Keep work running](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/SESSIONS)** Start a task and leave it running on your host. Your agent can continue its work when you close the client. Return later to review the results. **📱 [Work from any device](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/CONNECT)** Start on your desktop. Check progress from your phone. Open the same session in your browser or terminal. Your work stays in sync. **🤖 [Choose your agents](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/PLUGINS)** Use Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, pi, and other supported agents. Configure the agents you need and use them through one host. **🔑 [Subscriptions or API keys](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-claude)** Bring your existing agent subscriptions where supported, or connect model providers using your own API keys. Choose how you access and pay for AI. **🐳 [Run work in isolated environments](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/COMPUTERS)** Use Docker containers to give tasks their own environment. Keep work separate when projects need different tools or dependencies. **⏰ [Automate routine tasks](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/AUTOMATIONS)** Schedule agent work or start it from a webhook. Let your host run tasks even when no client is connected. Turn your agents into continuously available workers. **🔐 [Control access](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/USERS)** Control access to your agents and tools. Define who can interact with your host and what actions they can perform. Define permissions and usage policies for different users and teams. **📊 [Diagnostics](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/RUN#doctor)** Inspect host status, logs, network information, and telemetry. **💰 [Control spending](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/USAGE)** See what each person, team, and project has spent on models. Set daily, weekly, or monthly limits, and the host refuses new work when a limit is reached. **🔀 [Share your models](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/GATEWAY)** Point your agent or a script at your host and call any model with your ahpd token. The host uses the provider's key, applies your policies, and records the cost. Centralize credentials without distributing provider keys to every client. **🧩 [Extend with plugins](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/PLUGINS)** Add new agents, tools, integrations, and capabilities without rebuilding the server. Use existing plugins or build your own with the SDK. --- ## More than a chat With the right capabilities enabled, agents and clients can work with the same host resources. **📁 Resources** Read, write, create, and delete files through resource ports. **⌨️ Terminals** Open a shell on your host from any client. Watch the commands your agent runs as they run, and come back later to read their full output. **🌳 Git & GitHub** Inspect changes, branches, worktrees, and pull requests. Use separate worktrees to keep parallel sessions from sharing a working tree. --- ## Use the agents you prefer You do not need to commit to one agent or model provider. ahpd supports several agent integrations. Each integration runs as a plugin. [![@ahpd/agent-claude](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-claude?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-claude)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-claude) **✻ [`@ahpd/agent-claude`](packages/agent-claude/)**: Run Claude through the Claude Agent SDK. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-claude) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-claude ``` [![@ahpd/agent-pi](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-pi?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-pi)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-pi) **π [`@ahpd/agent-pi`](packages/agent-pi/)**: Run the pi coding agent directly in the host. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-pi) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-pi ``` [![@ahpd/agent-acp](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-acp?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-acp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-acp) **⇄ [`@ahpd/agent-acp`](packages/agent-acp/)**: Codex, Copilot, Gemini, and other supported agents through Agent Client Protocol. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-acp) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-acp ``` [![@ahpd/agent-cofold](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-cofold?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-cofold)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-cofold) **◈ [`@ahpd/agent-cofold`](packages/agent-cofold/)**: Generic harness to use supported OpenAI-compatible models. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-cofold) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-cofold ``` --- ## Add more with plugins Each capability can be configured to fit your environment. [![@ahpd/computer](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fcomputer?label=%40ahpd%2Fcomputer)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/computer) **[`@ahpd/computer`](packages/computer/)**: Create isolated environments for agentic tasks. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/computer) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/computer ``` [![@ahpd/bot](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fbot?label=%40ahpd%2Fbot)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/bot) **[`@ahpd/bot`](packages/bot/)**: Give an agent its own identity, workspace, and session. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/bot) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/bot ``` [![@ahpd/webhook](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fwebhook?label=%40ahpd%2Fwebhook)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/webhook) **[`@ahpd/webhook`](packages/webhook/)**: Start work from an HTTP request. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/webhook) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/webhook ``` [![@ahpd/tunnel-devtunnel](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Ftunnel-devtunnel?label=%40ahpd%2Ftunnel-devtunnel)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/tunnel-devtunnel) **[`@ahpd/tunnel-devtunnel`](packages/tunnel-devtunnel/)**: Reach your host from VS Code on another network, through a Microsoft Dev Tunnel. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/tunnel-devtunnel) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/tunnel-devtunnel ``` [![@ahpd/tasks](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Ftasks?label=%40ahpd%2Ftasks)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/tasks) **[`@ahpd/tasks`](packages/tasks/)**: Keep one list of tasks and plans that every agent and person reads and writes. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/tasks) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/tasks ``` [![@ahpd/push](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fpush?label=%40ahpd%2Fpush)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/push) **[`@ahpd/push`](packages/push/)**: Get a phone notification when a session needs you, with the app closed. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/push) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/push ``` [![@ahpd/activepieces](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Factivepieces?label=%40ahpd%2Factivepieces)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/activepieces) **[`@ahpd/activepieces`](packages/activepieces/)**: Use Activepieces connectors as tools for your sessions and bots. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/activepieces) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/activepieces ``` --- ## One host. Many clients. ahpd runs your agents and keeps their sessions. Connect with the client that suits you. ### 🌐 Browser → @ahpd/web Manage sessions, files, terminals, and host settings from your browser. [GitHub](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpw) · [Releases](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpw/releases) ### 🖥️ Desktop → ahp-desk Connect to multiple hosts, manage local installations, and work in dedicated windows. [GitHub](https://github.com/ahpio/ahp-desk) · [Download](https://github.com/ahpio/ahp-desk/releases) ### 💻 Terminal → @softov/ahpc Work with agents through an interactive terminal, CLI commands, or scripts. ```bash # Connect to your host with the terminal client npx @softov/ahpc --host --token ``` [GitHub](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpc) · [Releases](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpc/releases) ### 📱 Mobile → AgentHost Client Follow work, receive notifications, and respond when an agent needs your approval. [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.agenthostclient.app) · iOS soon · [Website](https://agenthostclient.com) ### 🔌 Other AHP clients Connect with compatible applications, including supported VS Code integrations. [AHP Client Libraries](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/guide/clients.html) · [AHP Implementations](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/guide/implementations.html) --- **One host, every screen.** Start work on one device and continue from another. Your sessions stay on the host. --- ## Make it your own ahpd has a small core and a plugin system. Add new agents, tools, URI schemes, environments, and services without modifying the daemon. ### 🧰 Build with the SDK [`@ahpd/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/sdk) lets you embed an AHP host in your application. It handles protocol negotiation, subscriptions, snapshots, state updates, reconnects, sessions, chats, and transcript paging. ```ts import { createHost, listen } from '@ahpd/sdk'; import { claude } from '@ahpd/agent-claude'; const path = process.cwd(); const host = createHost({ path, agents: [claude({ paths: [path] })] }); await listen({ port: 9187 }, (peer) => host.accept(peer)); ``` [Build your own host](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/BUILD-A-HOST) ### 🧩 Write plugins and agents You can extend your host without changing the server itself. Implement the `Agent` interface or contribute host ports, tools, and URI schemes. Load extensions from npm packages, local directories, or manifest-backed files. ```bash # Load plugins for one run, on top of the configured list ahpd --plugin @ahpd/agent-claude --plugin @ahpd/computer # A single file, with a plugin.json beside it that names its id and main ahpd --plugin ./scratch-agent.mjs # A directory with a manifest, tried against the working directory first ahpd --plugin ./my-custom-agent ``` A custom agent implements the same `Agent` interface and is named the same way as the agents above. A client speaks only AHP and depends on no agent SDK. ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef core fill:#0f172a,stroke:#10b981,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#fff classDef plugin fill:#1e293b,stroke:#8b5cf6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#fff classDef claude fill:#1e293b,stroke:#F88c00,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#fff classDef cofold fill:#1e293b,stroke:#3b82f6,stroke-width:1.5px,color:#fff SERVER["@ahpd/server"] SDK["@ahpd/sdk"] subgraph Plugins ["Agent Plugins"] CLAUDE["@ahpd/agent-claude"] COFOLD["@ahpd/agent-cofold"] ACP["@ahpd/agent-acp"] PI["@ahpd/agent-pi"] CUSTOM["Your agent"] end SERVER --> SDK SERVER -. "dynamically loads" .-> Plugins CLAUDE -->|"implements"| AGENT["Agent Interface"] COFOLD -->|"implements"| AGENT ACP -->|"implements"| AGENT PI -->|"implements"| AGENT CUSTOM -->|"implements"| AGENT SDK -->|"hosts & manages"| AGENT class SERVER,SDK core class CLAUDE claude class COFOLD cofold class ACP,PI,CUSTOM plugin ``` > Plugins execute inside the daemon with its permissions: install only code you trust. > Add the integrations you need. Remove or disable the ones you do not use. [Write a plugin](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/PLUGINS) · [Write an agent](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/AGENT) · [Smallest agent example](examples/echo) --- ## Documentation The full documentation is at [ahpio.github.io/ahpd](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/). | Document | Purpose | | --- | --- | | [Get started](docs/server/GET-STARTED.md) | Install, configure, start, and connect VS Code | | [Install](docs/server/INSTALL.md) | Install, and run on Node, Bun or Deno | | [Upgrade](docs/server/UPGRADE.md) | Upgrade the daemon and its plugins | | [Reference](docs/server/REFERENCE.md) | Every command and flag | | [Plugins](docs/server/PLUGINS.md) | Install, update, and configure plugins | | [Users](docs/server/USERS.md) | Users and authorization | | [Policy](docs/sdk/POLICY.md) | Who may use which agent, model and computer, and how much | | [Usage](docs/server/USAGE.md) | What each person, team and project has spent | | [Model gateway](docs/server/GATEWAY.md) | Call a model through the host with your ahpd token | | [Write a plugin](docs/plugins/PLUGINS.md) | The plugin contract, manifest and events | | [Write an agent](docs/sdk/AGENT.md) | The `Agent` and `Session` contracts | | [Build your own host](docs/sdk/BUILD-A-HOST.md) | `createHost` and the ports | | [AHP compatibility](docs/sdk/AHP.md) | What this host implements of AHP, command by command | Every document is listed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), one line each. Built on the [Agent Host Protocol (AHP)](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/). See [AHP compatibility](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/AHP) for what it implements. --- ## Development Tips, PRs, and contributions are welcome! Read [DEVELOPER.md](DEVELOPER.md) for detailed development guidelines. Discuss development, issues, and ideas on the [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd/discussions) page. Any development starts with cloning or forking the repository and installing dependencies. ```bash git clone https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd cd ahpd pnpm install pnpm build pnpm test pnpm typecheck ``` Protocol captures can be checked against the strict schema: ```bash pnpm wire -- packages/sdk/test/fixtures/wire.jsonl ``` --- ## Open source. Built for choice. ahpd is open source and released under the MIT license. Run it on your own infrastructure. Choose your agents, configure your tools, and build the environment that works for you. Use it for a personal project, a development team, or an application that needs agent capabilities. **Your infrastructure. Your agents. Your workflow.** ahpd is part of ahpio, the Agent Host Platform. Get to know the whole platform at [ahpio.com](https://ahpio.com). [Documentation](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd) · [ahpio.com](https://ahpio.com) > Sorry to beg, but if you find this project useful, consider starring the repository on GitHub.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# One run per branch. A push over a push is a run nobody is waiting for.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # The unit tests are split over two runners, because one runner took from
  # 223 s to 293 s for the same commit as runners vary, against the bound of 300.
  linux:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A hung test should fail the run rather than sit on a runner for six hours,
    # which is the default.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      # Every shard reports, so one red shard does not hide another.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2]
    name: linux (${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          # The `engines` field, and the version the tests are written against.
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      # Frozen, so a lockfile that does not match package.json fails here
      # rather than resolving to something nobody wrote down.
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # Before the tests: the boundary is the claim these packages make, and a
      # host that imports a backend is worth failing for even when it passes.
      # On one shard, because they do not depend on which tests it runs.
      - name: The packages import only what they declare
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: pnpm boundary

      # Each plugin's sdk range is the one this release sets: from its sdk to
      # the next minor. A bump that forgot it fails here, not at the tag.
      - name: Each plugin names the sdk range of this release
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: pnpm sdk-range

      # A catalog is keyed by field path, so a renamed field leaves an entry
      # nothing reads.
      - name: Each catalog path names a field
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: pnpm i18n

      - run: pnpm typecheck
        if: matrix.shard == 1

      # Bounded, because a job that runs into the runner's own timeout is
      # cancelled rather than failed, and a cancelled job leaves no readable
      # log at all - which is how a shell test killing this process group came
      # to look like a hang for an afternoon.
      - name: Tests
        run: timeout 450 pnpm test:unit --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/2

      # Last, because it is the slowest and the only one that writes anything.
      - run: pnpm build
        if: matrix.shard == 1

      # What would actually be published, which is not what `files` says until
      # something has packed it: `ahpd` ships no `src`, the libraries do.
      - name: Pack each package
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: pnpm -r exec pnpm pack --pack-destination ${{ runner.temp }}

  # The check the `main` ruleset requires by this name: green only when every
  # Linux shard is, and red when one failed, was cancelled or never ran.
  check:
    needs: linux
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: test "${{ needs.linux.result }}" = success

  # The same checks on Windows. Every step runs under bash, so this is the same
  # commands as `linux` rather than a second version of them. The tests are split
  # over four runners, because the whole run takes from 390 s to 590 s on one
  # as runners vary, and a bound it runs into reports no failures at all.
  windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      # Every shard reports, so one red shard does not hide another.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    name: windows (${{ matrix.shard }}/4)
    steps:
      # Before the checkout: some paths under `.project/plans` are 185
      # characters long, and with the checkout folder in front they pass the 260
      # a Windows path may have, and the checkout fails with "Filename too long".
      - run: git config --global core.longpaths true
        shell: bash

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        shell: bash

      # On one shard, because they do not depend on which tests it runs.
      - name: The packages import only what they declare
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: pnpm boundary
        shell: bash

      - name: Each plugin names the sdk range of this release
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: pnpm sdk-range
        shell: bash

      - run: pnpm typecheck
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        shell: bash

      # A git call over 2 s is written to stderr, so a case that stalls on this
      # runner names the call in its log.
      - name: Tests
        run: timeout 450 pnpm test:unit --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4
        shell: bash
        env:
          AHPD_GIT_SLOW_MS: '2000'

      # The computer plugin's cases that need no Docker, which `processes`
      # runs on Linux only: its Windows paths run nowhere else. The cases that
      # start a real container skip, because this runner's engine runs no
      # Linux image.
      - name: Computer tests
        run: timeout 450 pnpm exec vitest run packages/computer/ --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4
        shell: bash

      # Last, because it is the slowest and the only one that writes anything.
      # `linux` packs each package after this step and this job does not: what a
      # package would publish is one answer, and Linux's is it.
      - run: pnpm build
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        shell: bash

  # The check the `main` ruleset requires by this name: green only when every
  # Windows shard is, and red when one failed, was cancelled or never ran.
  check-windows:
    needs: windows
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - run: test "${{ needs.windows.result }}" = success

  # The cases that start real processes and Docker containers: the daemon's
  # command line, the HTTP server, the computer plugin and a nested host. They
  # are most of the test time, so they run beside `linux` on runners of their
  # own, under the same bound, split over two because one runner took from 208 s
  # to past 300 s for the same commit.
  processes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      # Every shard reports, so one red shard does not hide another.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2]
    name: processes (${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Tests
        run: timeout 450 pnpm test:processes --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/2

  # `resourceWrite` is symmetrical, so this host implements the whole of it and
  # so does `ahpc`. `packages/sdk/test/fixtures/resource-write.json` is the same file in both
  # repositories and each runs it against its own implementation - which catches
  # a behavioural divergence, but not a case added on one side and never copied
  # to the other. This is what catches that.
  fixture:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: The write fixture matches ahpc's copy
        run: |
          set -u
          url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahpio/ahpc/main/test/fixtures/resource-write.json
          code=$(curl -sS -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/theirs.json" -w '%{http_code}' "$url")
          if [ "$code" = "404" ]; then
            # Not landed over there yet. Said rather than failed, because the
            # two repositories are pushed one at a time and a red build for the
            # gap between them would be a build nobody could make green.
            echo "ahpc's main has no copy of this fixture yet. Nothing to compare."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
            echo "Could not read ahpc's copy: HTTP $code"
            exit 1
          fi
          diff -u "$RUNNER_TEMP/theirs.json" packages/sdk/test/fixtures/resource-write.json && echo "The two copies are identical."

  # The one-line install, run where a person reads it: a clean container with no
  # Node, one with a Node older than the engine floor, and one at the floor. The
  # two without a new enough Node must stop and print the nvm command instead of
  # installing something the daemon cannot run on.
  install:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - image: debian:12-slim
            outcome: stops
          - image: node:20-bookworm-slim
            outcome: stops
          - image: node:22-bookworm-slim
            outcome: installs
    container:
      image: ${{ matrix.image }}
    steps:
      # Before the checkout: none of the slim images ships git, and the Debian
      # one ships no curl either, and the checkout action asks for git first.
      - name: Tools the base image does not have
        run: apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git curl ca-certificates

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: The install runs
        if: matrix.outcome == 'installs'
        run: bash scripts/install/install.sh --no-onboard

      - name: Without a new enough Node it stops
        if: matrix.outcome == 'stops'
        run: |
          set -u
          if bash scripts/install/install.sh --no-onboard > "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log" 2>&1; then
            echo "It installed without Node 22.1."
            cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log"
            exit 1
          fi
          cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log"
          grep -F 'nvm install 22' "$RUNNER_TEMP/install.log"

      - name: ahpd runs
        if: matrix.outcome == 'installs'
        run: ahpd --version

      - name: The uninstall removes it again
        if: matrix.outcome == 'installs'
        run: |
          set -u
          bash scripts/install/install.sh --uninstall
          if command -v ahpd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "ahpd is still on the PATH."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -f "$HOME/.profile" ] && grep -F '# added by the ahpd install script' "$HOME/.profile"; then
            echo "The PATH line is still there."
            exit 1
          fi

  # Every PR builds the image a release publishes, and runs the checks a
  # person's upgrade depends on: the state lives in the volume and outlives a
  # restart, a new container and an image swap. The build is cached by buildx,
  # so a run that changed nothing outside the image packs nothing again.
  image:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4

      - name: Build the image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          file: Dockerfile
          load: true
          tags: ahpd:dev
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      # By bash rather than by its own mode, so the check does not depend on
      # the mode the file was committed with.
      - name: The checks
        run: bash docker/test/smoke.sh ahpd:dev

      # The same build from the URL a person uses. On a fork's pull request
      # this is the fork's own repository and commit, so the fork's code is
      # what is built and not the base repository's.
      - name: Build from the pull request's GitHub URL
        run: |
          set -eu
          repository=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name || github.repository }}
          commit=${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          docker build -t ahpd:from-git "https://github.com/$repository.git#$commit"

  # The Windows one-line install: once with a Node at the floor, and once with
  # no Node on the PATH at all, where it must stop with the winget command
  # rather than install something the daemon cannot run on.
  install-windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22

      - name: The install runs
        shell: pwsh
        run: ./scripts/install/install.ps1 -NoOnboard

      # The runner hands each step its own environment and does not read the
      # user PATH back from the registry, so the folder the install wrote is
      # named here. The test suite is what checks that the entry is in the PATH
      # for a new session.
      - name: ahpd runs
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $folder = (& npm prefix -g).Trim()
          $env:PATH = "$folder;$env:PATH"
          ahpd --version

      - name: The uninstall removes it again
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          & ./scripts/install/install.ps1 -Uninstall
          $folder = (& npm prefix -g).Trim()
          if (Test-Path (Join-Path $folder 'ahpd.cmd')) {
            throw 'ahpd is still installed.'
          }

      - name: Without Node it stops with the winget command
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $env:PATH = "$env:SystemRoot\System32;$env:SystemRoot"
          $installed = $true
          $message = ''
          try {
            & ./scripts/install/install.ps1 -NoOnboard
          } catch {
            $installed = $false
            $message = "$_"
          }
          if ($installed) {
            throw 'It installed without Node.'
          }
          if ($message -notmatch 'winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS') {
            throw "Unexpected failure: $message"
          }
sampled_files.Dockerfile:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

# The ahpd image: @ahpd/server from this checkout, run by a person who has
# Docker and nothing else.
#
# Three stages. `pack` builds and packs the workspace the way release.yml does,
# `install` puts the server and its sibling packages into a prefix with
# node-pty compiled, and `runtime` carries that prefix and none of the
# toolchain. The same build serves `docker build .` from a checkout and
# `docker build https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd.git#<ref>` from Git.

ARG NODE_IMAGE=node:22-bookworm-slim

# 1. Pack -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# pnpm packs, never npm: these packages depend on each other with `workspace:^`
# and only pnpm rewrites that to a real range on the way out.
FROM ${NODE_IMAGE} AS pack

# A corepack that asks before it downloads pnpm would stop a build with no
# terminal to answer it.
ENV COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0

WORKDIR /src

COPY . .

RUN corepack enable \
 && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile \
 && pnpm build \
 && mkdir -p /out \
 && pnpm -r exec pnpm pack --pack-destination /out

# 2. Install ----------------------------------------------------------------
#
# node-pty is an optional dependency of @ahpd/server and builds from source
# here, so the image has the compiler the install needs.
FROM ${NODE_IMAGE} AS install

RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends python3 make g++ \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

COPY --from=pack /out /tmp/pack

# npm 12 skips install scripts by default, so node-pty's build runs only when
# the flag that allows it is passed. npm 11.16 is the first that knows the
# flag; an older npm runs the script anyway and is given no flag it would
# refuse. This is the rule selfupdate.ts applies to the update it runs.
RUN set -eu; \
    allow=''; \
    version=$(npm --version); \
    major=${version%%.*}; \
    rest=${version#*.}; \
    minor=${rest%%.*}; \
    if [ "$major" -gt 11 ] || { [ "$major" -eq 11 ] && [ "$minor" -ge 16 ]; }; then \
      allow='--allow-scripts=node-pty'; \
    fi; \
    echo "npm $version, allow-scripts: ${allow:-no}"; \
    npm install -g --prefix /opt/ahpd $allow \
      /tmp/pack/ahpd-server-*.tgz /tmp/pack/ahpd-sdk-*.tgz

# 3. Runtime ----------------------------------------------------------------
FROM ${NODE_IMAGE} AS runtime

# uid 1000 is the first ordinary user on a Linux host, so a folder a person
# owns there is writable here without a chown. Compose `user:` sets another.
ARG AHPD_UID=1000
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG REVISION=unknown
ARG SOURCE=https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="ahpd" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="An Agent Host Protocol server for Claude, pi, ACP agents and any agent a plugin adds" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${REVISION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.source="${SOURCE}"

# git and ssh for the computers and the sessions; bash for the shells a session
# runs; tini as PID 1, so a stop reaches ahpd and a dead child is reaped;
# procps for `ps` in a session.
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      git bash ca-certificates openssh-client tini procps \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# The base image's `node` user, under the name this image runs as.
RUN groupmod -n ahpd node \
 && usermod -l ahpd -d /home/ahpd -m node \
 && usermod -u "${AHPD_UID}" ahpd \
 && mkdir -p /home/ahpd/.npm-global/bin /work \
 && chown -R ahpd:ahpd /home/ahpd /work

# root owns the code. A session that writes here would change the image rather
# than the volume, and a container that writes its own program is one whose
# next start disagrees with what was built.
COPY --from=install /opt/ahpd /opt/ahpd

# The script is the repository's file, copied rather than installed, so the
# image and the checkout run the same one. root owns it beside the code.
COPY --chmod=0755 docker/entrypoint.sh /opt/ahpd/entrypoint.sh

ENV PATH=/opt/ahpd/bin:/home/ahpd/.npm-global/bin:$PATH \
    NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=/home/ahpd/.npm-global \
    AHPD_SERVICE=container

WORKDIR /work
VOLUME ["/home/ahpd"]
EXPOSE 9187
USER ahpd

# A daemon that is recorded is one a client can reach. With no record the
# command exits non-zero, which is the unhealthy answer.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=120s --retries=3 \
  CMD ahpd status --json

ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--", "/opt/ahpd/entrypoint.sh"]

# 0.0.0.0 inside the container reaches only whoever publishes the port, and it
# forces a token. The token lives in the volume and is read from a file, so it
# is never a flag in `docker inspect`.
CMD ["run", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "9187", \
     "--connection-token-file", "/home/ahpd/.config/ahpd/connection-token", \
     "--path", "/work", "--no-cwd"]

sampled_files.README.md:
# ahpd - agent host platform [![CI](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![@ahpd/server](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fserver?label=%40ahpd%2Fserver)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/server) [![@ahpd/sdk](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fsdk?label=%40ahpd%2Fsdk)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/sdk) [![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-ahpio.github.io%2Fahpd-0b7285)](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/) ![license MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue) ![node >=22](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22-5fa04e) ![Agent Host Protocol 1.1.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/AHP-1.1.0-0b7285) ![runs on Node, Bun, Deno](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20on-Node%20%7C%20Bun%20%7C%20Deno-495057) **Run your AI agents anywhere. Control them from anywhere.** `ahpd` is an open-source, self-hosted platform that brings multiple AI agents together. Run Claude Code SDK, Pi SDK, ACP agents (Codex, Copilot, Gemini, and more), or your own custom harness using supported subscriptions or API keys. Extend their capabilities with plugins, tools, connectors, MCP servers, and integrations. Schedule tasks or run sessions on your computer, remote servers, or in containers, with full control over your environments and resources. Whether it's for personal use or an organization, manage access, monitor usage, and control budgets from one place. Connect from your browser, desktop, terminal, or phone. Your sessions and work stay in sync across every client. > It also has a `shared editing` feature for real-time collaboration. > > **And this is just the beginning.** ahpd is an extensible platform, built to grow with new agents, integrations, and possibilities. [Read the documentation](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/) · [GitHub](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd) · [Discord](https://discord.gg/NWvnuqEQxG) [ahpio.com](https://ahpio.com)

--- ## Start in minutes Install with one line on Linux or macOS: ```bash curl -fsSL https://ahpio.com/ahpd/install.sh | bash ``` On Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://ahpio.com/ahpd/install.ps1 | iex ``` The script checks for Node 22.18 or newer, installs `@ahpd/server` without sudo, adds `ahpd` to your PATH, and runs `ahpd configure`. [Install options](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/INSTALL) Or install with npm, then run the setup: ```bash npm install -g @ahpd/server --allow-scripts=node-pty ahpd configure ``` Choose your agents, network settings, and project folders. To add an agent later, run `ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-claude`. Start the host: ```bash ahpd start --path /work/project ``` Your host is ready for an AHP client. Connect from the terminal with ahpc: ```bash npx @softov/ahpc --host ws://127.0.0.1:9187 ``` ### 🗂️ Serve multiple projects ```bash ahpd --path /work/api --path /work/web ``` Project paths are catalogue entries, **not filesystem sandboxes**. Access to other paths depends on the configured host capabilities and permissions. ### 🔐 Connect remotely By default, the host listens on loopback. To listen on another interface, configure a connection token: ```bash ahpd --host 0.0.0.0 --connection-token-file ~/.config/ahpd/token ``` Only expose the host to networks you trust, and protect the token. See the [remote access documentation](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/REMOTE). --- ## Your agents. Your machines. Your control. Run the agents you prefer, manage how they work, and stay in control of your infrastructure, access, and spending. AI agents can help you write code, fix problems, manage files, and automate tasks. But they often depend on the terminal or application where you started them. ahpd gives your agents a place to run and gives you a way to reach them. **⏳ [Keep work running](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/SESSIONS)** Start a task and leave it running on your host. Your agent can continue its work when you close the client. Return later to review the results. **📱 [Work from any device](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/CONNECT)** Start on your desktop. Check progress from your phone. Open the same session in your browser or terminal. Your work stays in sync. **🤖 [Choose your agents](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/PLUGINS)** Use Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, pi, and other supported agents. Configure the agents you need and use them through one host. **🔑 [Subscriptions or API keys](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-claude)** Bring your existing agent subscriptions where supported, or connect model providers using your own API keys. Choose how you access and pay for AI. **🐳 [Run work in isolated environments](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/COMPUTERS)** Use Docker containers to give tasks their own environment. Keep work separate when projects need different tools or dependencies. **⏰ [Automate routine tasks](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/AUTOMATIONS)** Schedule agent work or start it from a webhook. Let your host run tasks even when no client is connected. Turn your agents into continuously available workers. **🔐 [Control access](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/USERS)** Control access to your agents and tools. Define who can interact with your host and what actions they can perform. Define permissions and usage policies for different users and teams. **📊 [Diagnostics](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/RUN#doctor)** Inspect host status, logs, network information, and telemetry. **💰 [Control spending](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/USAGE)** See what each person, team, and project has spent on models. Set daily, weekly, or monthly limits, and the host refuses new work when a limit is reached. **🔀 [Share your models](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/server/GATEWAY)** Point your agent or a script at your host and call any model with your ahpd token. The host uses the provider's key, applies your policies, and records the cost. Centralize credentials without distributing provider keys to every client. **🧩 [Extend with plugins](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/PLUGINS)** Add new agents, tools, integrations, and capabilities without rebuilding the server. Use existing plugins or build your own with the SDK. --- ## More than a chat With the right capabilities enabled, agents and clients can work with the same host resources. **📁 Resources** Read, write, create, and delete files through resource ports. **⌨️ Terminals** Open a shell on your host from any client. Watch the commands your agent runs as they run, and come back later to read their full output. **🌳 Git & GitHub** Inspect changes, branches, worktrees, and pull requests. Use separate worktrees to keep parallel sessions from sharing a working tree. --- ## Use the agents you prefer You do not need to commit to one agent or model provider. ahpd supports several agent integrations. Each integration runs as a plugin. [![@ahpd/agent-claude](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-claude?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-claude)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-claude) **✻ [`@ahpd/agent-claude`](packages/agent-claude/)**: Run Claude through the Claude Agent SDK. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-claude) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-claude ``` [![@ahpd/agent-pi](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-pi?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-pi)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-pi) **π [`@ahpd/agent-pi`](packages/agent-pi/)**: Run the pi coding agent directly in the host. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-pi) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-pi ``` [![@ahpd/agent-acp](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-acp?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-acp)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-acp) **⇄ [`@ahpd/agent-acp`](packages/agent-acp/)**: Codex, Copilot, Gemini, and other supported agents through Agent Client Protocol. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-acp) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-acp ``` [![@ahpd/agent-cofold](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fagent-cofold?label=%40ahpd%2Fagent-cofold)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/agent-cofold) **◈ [`@ahpd/agent-cofold`](packages/agent-cofold/)**: Generic harness to use supported OpenAI-compatible models. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/agent-cofold) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/agent-cofold ``` --- ## Add more with plugins Each capability can be configured to fit your environment. [![@ahpd/computer](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fcomputer?label=%40ahpd%2Fcomputer)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/computer) **[`@ahpd/computer`](packages/computer/)**: Create isolated environments for agentic tasks. [docs](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/bot) ```bash ahpd plugin install @ahpd/bot ``` [![@ahpd/webhook](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/%40ahpd%2Fwebhook?label=%40ahpd%2Fwebhook)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ahpd/webhook) **[`@ahpd/webhook`](packages/webhook/)**: Start work from an HTTP request. Remove or disable the ones you do not use. [Write a plugin](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/plugins/PLUGINS) · [Write an agent](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/AGENT) · [Smallest agent example](examples/echo) --- ## Documentation The full documentation is at [ahpio.github.io/ahpd](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/). | Document | Purpose | | --- | --- | | [Get started](docs/server/GET-STARTED.md) | Install, configure, start, and connect VS Code | | [Install](docs/server/INSTALL.md) | Install, and run on Node, Bun or Deno | | [Upgrade](docs/server/UPGRADE.md) | Upgrade the daemon and its plugins | | [Reference](docs/server/REFERENCE.md) | Every command and flag | | [Plugins](docs/server/PLUGINS.md) | Install, update, and configure plugins | | [Users](docs/server/USERS.md) | Users and authorization | | [Policy](docs/sdk/POLICY.md) | Who may use which agent, model and computer, and how much | | [Usage](docs/server/USAGE.md) | What each person, team and project has spent | | [Model gateway](docs/server/GATEWAY.md) | Call a model through the host with your ahpd token | | [Write a plugin](docs/plugins/PLUGINS.md) | The plugin contract, manifest and events | | [Write an agent](docs/sdk/AGENT.md) | The `Agent` and `Session` contracts | | [Build your own host](docs/sdk/BUILD-A-HOST.md) | `createHost` and the ports | | [AHP compatibility](docs/sdk/AHP.md) | What this host implements of AHP, command by command | Every document is listed in [docs/README.md](docs/README.md), one line each. Built on the [Agent Host Protocol (AHP)](https://microsoft.github.io/agent-host-protocol/). See [AHP compatibility](https://ahpio.github.io/ahpd/sdk/AHP) for what it implements. --- ## Development Tips, PRs, and contributions are welcome! Read [DEVELOPER.md](DEVELOPER.md) for detailed development guidelines. Discuss development, issues, and ideas on the [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd/discussions) page. Any development starts with cloning or forking the repository and installing dependencies. ```bash git clone https://github.com/ahpio/ahpd cd ahpd pnpm install pnpm build pnpm test pnpm typecheck ``` Protocol captures can be checked against the strict schema: ```bash pnpm wire -- packages/sdk/test/fixtures/wire.jsonl ``` --- ## Open source. Built for choice. ahpd is open source and released under the MIT license. Run it on your own infrastructure. Choose your agents, configure your tools, and build the environment that works for you.
