name: CI

permissions:
  contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      refresh_baseline:
        description: "Regenerate the quality-gate baseline (cases.json + baseline_replay.json) and upload it as an artifact instead of running the check."
        type: boolean
        default: false
      refresh_retrieval_baselines:
        description: "Regenerate the retrieval-eval baselines (baseline_v0.3.8.json + baseline_v2.json) on Ubuntu and upload them as an artifact instead of running the floor checks."
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # schedule:
  #   - cron: "17 5 * * *"   # nightly — enable once LLM secrets are provisioned

# Single source of truth for the uv toolchain setup-uv installs. Pinning (vs
# "latest") keeps CI reproducible; Dependabot's github-actions updater can't
# touch a `with:` input, so bump this by hand — in lockstep with the same pin
# in release.yml, release-langchain.yml, release-sbom.yml and
# release-langchain-sbom.yml.
env:
  UV_VERSION: "0.11.16"
  # A CI runner has no owner for ~/.claude/settings.json and its siblings
  # besides the suite itself, so a change the in-process write witness cannot
  # attribute is still a leak here and must fail. Developer machines, where an
  # editor session writes those files concurrently, default to a summary line
  # instead of blaming whichever test happened to be in flight (#2355).
  MEMTOMEM_TEST_HOME_GUARD: strict

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      # Fail closed on pyproject <-> uv.lock drift (e.g. a Dependabot member-dep
      # update that edits the lock's requires-dist but not the member manifest).
      # dependabot.yml uses versioning-strategy: lockfile-only to prevent that at
      # the source; this is the CI backstop, since every other job resolves with
      # `uv sync --frozen` (which neither checks nor regenerates the lock).
      - run: uv lock --check
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run ruff check packages/memtomem/src packages/memtomem/tests packages/langchain-memtomem/src packages/langchain-memtomem/tests packages/memtomem-hermes-memory/*.py tools examples/onboarding/slateharbor/*.py examples/workflows/*.py
      - run: uv run ruff format --check packages/memtomem/src packages/memtomem/tests packages/langchain-memtomem/src packages/langchain-memtomem/tests packages/memtomem-hermes-memory/*.py tools examples/onboarding/slateharbor/*.py examples/workflows/*.py

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - name: mypy (gradual)
        run: uv run mypy packages/memtomem/src packages/langchain-memtomem/src

  # Linux and macOS run the suite in cost-balanced shards, like Windows: run
  # whole, each was the run's critical path at 24-25 minutes, ahead of the
  # Windows shards' 16-19 while every required check outside the test suite
  # finished in 3, and strict up-to-date merging pays that again on every
  # update-branch. One job per OS rather than one os x shard matrix,
  # because `needs.<job>.result` is a single result for a whole matrix, so a
  # macOS failure would also turn `test (ubuntu-latest)` red. Keep each job's
  # shard list and --shard-count in step.
  test-ubuntu-shard:
    name: ubuntu-test-shard (${{ matrix.shard }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      # Pinned to what the runner image had been providing, Ubuntu's system
      # 3.12; see the macOS job for why an unpinned interpreter broke.
      - run: uv python pin 3.12
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: >-
          uv run python tools/run_pytest_shard.py
          --shard-index ${{ matrix.shard }}
          --shard-count 2 --
          -m "not ollama and not llm"
          --tb=short -q

  test-ubuntu:
    name: test (ubuntu-latest)
    if: ${{ always() }}
    needs: [test-ubuntu-shard]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Require every Linux shard to succeed
        env:
          SHARD_RESULT: ${{ needs.test-ubuntu-shard.result }}
        run: test "$SHARD_RESULT" = success

  test-macos-shard:
    name: macos-test-shard (${{ matrix.shard }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      # Pinned to what the runner image had been providing, Homebrew's 3.14.
      # Unpinned, uv uses an interpreter it discovers on the image, and
      # macos-26-arm64 20261013 moved Homebrew's default to 3.15, for which
      # onnxruntime 1.24.4 has no wheel, so `uv sync` failed before any test
      # ran.
      - run: uv python pin 3.14
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: >-
          uv run python tools/run_pytest_shard.py
          --shard-index ${{ matrix.shard }}
          --shard-count 2 --
          -m "not ollama and not llm"
          --tb=short -q

  test-macos:
    name: test (macos-latest)
    if: ${{ always() }}
    needs: [test-macos-shard]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Require every macOS shard to succeed
        env:
          SHARD_RESULT: ${{ needs.test-macos-shard.result }}
        run: test "$SHARD_RESULT" = success

  test-windows-shard:
    name: windows-test-shard (${{ matrix.shard }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2, 3]
    runs-on: windows-latest
    # 35, matching the Linux and macOS shards, and a hang guard (#1642) that
    # still fires long before the 6-hour default. Three shards, not two
    # (#2720): with two, the heavier shard's job ran 25-28 minutes, and a
    # Windows runner 1.4x slow pushed one past 35 at 96% done. Four, not
    # three, once Linux and macOS were sharded: at three the heaviest Windows
    # shard (16-19 minutes) became the run's critical path. Keep the shard
    # list and --shard-count below in step.
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: >-
          uv run python tools/run_pytest_shard.py
          --shard-index ${{ matrix.shard }}
          --shard-count 4 --
          -m "not ollama and not llm"
          --tb=short -q
          --junit-xml=junit-windows-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Per-file Windows timings, the input for regenerating the shard cost map
      # with `tools/run_pytest_shard.py --record-durations` (one report per
      # shard). `!cancelled()` uploads after a passed or a failed pytest step.
      # What a shard stopped by the job timeout leaves behind is not relied on.
      - name: Upload shard timings
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: junit-windows-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: junit-windows-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 14

  test-windows:
    name: test (windows-latest)
    if: ${{ always() }}
    needs: [test-windows-shard]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Require every Windows shard to succeed
        env:
          SHARD_RESULT: ${{ needs.test-windows-shard.result }}
        run: test "$SHARD_RESULT" = success

  test-browser:
    name: browser (Playwright + Chromium)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      # ``--with-deps`` pulls the headless-shell apt packages on Ubuntu so
      # chromium can launch from a clean runner; the install also seeds the
      # browser cache that ``_playwright_browser_available()`` probes.
      - run: uv run playwright install --with-deps chromium
      # The probe in tests/conftest.py skips every browser test when Chromium
      # cannot launch, and pytest passes a run that skipped everything it
      # selected. Here that is a failure, with the launch error in the log (#3453).
      - run: uv run pytest packages/memtomem/tests/web -m browser --tb=short -q
        env:
          MEMTOMEM_TEST_REQUIRE_BROWSER: "1"

  test-golden-path:
    name: golden-path (ONNX)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/.fastembed-cache
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - name: Cache retrieval models (English bge-small + multilingual MiniLM)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-fastembed-retrieval-v2-bge-small-en-multilingual-minilm
      # Same pin as the producer job below. `requires-python` is `>=3.12` and
      # no `.python-version` is committed, so without this the runner could
      # hand the *checks* a different interpreter — and a different SQLite —
      # than the one that measured the floors they check.
      - run: uv python pin 3.12
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run pytest packages/memtomem/tests/test_golden_path.py --tb=short -q
      - name: Audit public synthetic retrieval corpus
        run: uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/audit_public_corpus.py
      # A baseline edited without regenerating its manifest is exactly the
      # shape the manifest exists to rule out, so the hashes are checked here
      # rather than trusted.
      - name: Verify baseline provenance
        run: |
          uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/write_provenance.py \
            --output tools/retrieval-eval/PROVENANCE.json --check
      - name: Check public retrieval quality floors
        env:
          PYTHONHASHSEED: "0"
          OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        run: uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/check_baseline.py --runs 1
      - name: Check language-separated retrieval v2 floors
        env:
          PYTHONHASHSEED: "0"
          OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        run: uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/check_baseline_v2.py

  # Canonical producer for the retrieval-eval baselines, the same contract the
  # quality gate has had since #1837. These floors are *checked* on Ubuntu, so
  # they must be *produced* on Ubuntu: the platform delta is the size of the
  # margins they are built from (#2224 — a macOS recalibration RAISED
  # ko|genre_primary|mrr@10 to 0.31 while this runner observed 0.291).
  #
  # Its own job, not a step in golden-path: it runs ten calibration passes plus
  # the v2 RRF grid, which needs a far larger timeout than the floor checks
  # should ever be allowed. Being a separate job also means a failing floor
  # cannot block its own refresh — nothing here `needs:` golden-path.
  retrieval-baselines-refresh:
    name: retrieval baselines (canonical refresh)
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.refresh_retrieval_baselines }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    env:
      FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/.fastembed-cache
      # Job-level, not per-step: these are properties of the measurement, and
      # the provenance step records them. Setting them only on the regenerate
      # step made the manifest report "unset" for a run that had them set.
      PYTHONHASHSEED: "0"
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - name: Cache retrieval models (English bge-small + multilingual MiniLM)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-fastembed-retrieval-v2-bge-small-en-multilingual-minilm
      # Pin the interpreter for the same reason the quality gate does: a
      # refresh has to reproduce the assets it replaces.
      - run: uv python pin 3.12
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - name: Regenerate both baselines
        run: |
          uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/calibrate_portfolio.py \
            --runs 10 --factor 0.85 --output tools/retrieval-eval/baseline_v0.3.8.json
          uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/tune_rrf_v2.py \
            --output tools/retrieval-eval/baseline_v2.json
      # A lowered floor is a claim; this is what lets someone audit it later.
      - name: Record provenance
        env:
          MEMTOMEM_PROVENANCE_COMMIT: ${{ github.sha }}
          MEMTOMEM_PROVENANCE_RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          uv run python tools/retrieval-eval/write_provenance.py \
            --output tools/retrieval-eval/PROVENANCE.json
      - name: Upload regenerated retrieval baselines
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: retrieval-eval-baselines
          path: |
            tools/retrieval-eval/baseline_v0.3.8.json
            tools/retrieval-eval/baseline_v2.json
            tools/retrieval-eval/PROVENANCE.json

  quality-gate:
    name: quality-gate (BM25 replay)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      # Ubuntu is the canonical baseline producer; pin the interpreter so a
      # workflow_dispatch refresh reproduces the committed assets (see
      # tools/quality-gate/README.md). The check step also benefits from it.
      - run: uv python pin 3.12
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      # Required: a policy violation fails the PR. The advisory introduction
      # window (#1837) closed with no mac↔Ubuntu ranking drift across PR-B, the
      # Ubuntu baseline regen, and unrelated PRs, so the gate now blocks.
      # Thresholds live in policy.json, never here; refresh the baseline in the
      # same PR as any intended ranking change (see tools/quality-gate/README.md).
      - name: Replay quality gate
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.refresh_baseline) }}
        env:
          PYTHONHASHSEED: "0"
          OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        run: uv run python tools/quality-gate/run_gate.py
      # Canonical refresh: regenerate the assets on Ubuntu and upload them for a
      # maintainer to review + commit. Records the Python + SQLite versions.
      - name: Refresh canonical baseline
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.refresh_baseline }}
        env:
          PYTHONHASHSEED: "0"
          OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        run: |
          uv run python tools/quality-gate/run_gate.py --refresh-baseline
          uv run python -c "import sqlite3, sys; open('tools/quality-gate/versions.txt', 'w').write(f'python={sys.version.split()[0]}\nsqlite={sqlite3.sqlite_version}\n')"
      - name: Upload regenerated baseline
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.refresh_baseline }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: quality-gate-baseline
          path: |
            tools/quality-gate/cases.json
            tools/quality-gate/baseline_replay.json
            tools/quality-gate/versions.txt

  test-llm-nightly:
    name: llm-nightly (optional)
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run pytest -m "llm" --tb=short -q

  notebooks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      - run: uv run pytest packages/memtomem/tests/test_notebooks.py --tb=short -q
      - name: Execute model-free beginner notebooks in a minimal environment
        run: |
          # 05/06 stay in a [langgraph]-only environment: that is the install
          # their own setup section documents, and sharing an environment with
          # 00 would let an accidental tree-sitter import in them pass here.
          uv venv /tmp/beginner-notebooks
          uv pip install --python /tmp/beginner-notebooks/bin/python -e 'packages/memtomem[langgraph]' nbclient ipykernel
          /tmp/beginner-notebooks/bin/python tools/check_beginner_notebooks.py --notebook 05_langgraph_memory_basics.ipynb --json
          /tmp/beginner-notebooks/bin/python tools/check_beginner_notebooks.py --notebook 06_langgraph_retrieval_memory.ipynb --json
          /tmp/beginner-notebooks/bin/python examples/onboarding/retry-policy/demo.py
          /tmp/beginner-notebooks/bin/python -m unittest discover -s examples/onboarding/retry-policy
          # 00 and the Slateharbor sample need the code extra for tree-sitter.
          uv venv /tmp/first-user-notebook
          uv pip install --python /tmp/first-user-notebook/bin/python -e 'packages/memtomem[code]' nbclient ipykernel
          /tmp/first-user-notebook/bin/python tools/check_beginner_notebooks.py --notebook 00_start_here.ipynb --json
          /tmp/first-user-notebook/bin/python examples/onboarding/slateharbor/generate.py --check
          /tmp/first-user-notebook/bin/python examples/onboarding/slateharbor/build_notebook.py --check
          /tmp/first-user-notebook/bin/python examples/onboarding/slateharbor/validate.py --json
      - name: Validate model-free workflow packages
        # Reuse the previous step's [code] venv. Two stores exercise isolation.
        run: /tmp/first-user-notebook/bin/python examples/workflows/demo.py --validate

  test-js:
    name: js-unit (vitest + jsdom)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/memtomem/tests-js
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      # Node 20 is below the floor the jsdom 30 line requires
      # (`^22.22.2 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0`, and its undici dependency needs
      # >=22.19.0) — `npm ci` only warns EBADENGINE there and the whole suite
      # then dies at import time. The range, rather than a bare "24", is
      # load-bearing: with check-latest off setup-node takes the newest
      # matching version already in the runner tool cache, which can be a 24.x
      # below jsdom's 24.15.0 floor.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v6
        with:
          node-version: "^24.15.0"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: packages/memtomem/tests-js/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

  test-opencode-plugin:
    name: OpenCode plugin (build + unit + pack)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: packages/opencode-memtomem
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v6
        with:
          node-version: "24"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: packages/opencode-memtomem/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run pack:check

  hermes-memory-py311:
    # Hermes Agent supports Python 3.11 while this monorepo targets 3.12, so the
    # memtomem-memory provider (packages/memtomem-hermes-memory) is written for 3.11.
    # A syntax check cannot see a 3.12-only standard-library API; this runs one recall
    # turn through the provider under a real 3.11 against the fake Hermes modules.
    name: hermes-memory (Python 3.11 smoke)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv run --no-project --python 3.11 python tools/hermes_memory_py311_smoke.py --repo-root .

  packaging-smoke:
    # Mirrors the wheel-install half of the release preflight so a dependency
    # bump that breaks an extra's install or import fails here, on the PR,
    # instead of at tag time when the release is already in flight (#2071).
    name: packaging-smoke (wheel + all extras)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - name: Every distribution an extra installs has a probe
        # --with packaging: only the coverage check parses PEP 508, and it
        # only ever runs here, from the checkout. packaging is a workspace
        # dev dependency, NOT a memtomem runtime one, so the probe run in
        # the isolated [all] venv below must not need it — see the lazy
        # import in the helper.
        run: uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with packaging python
          tools/extras_import_smoke.py --check-coverage --repo-root .
      - name: Build wheel
        run: uv build packages/memtomem --out-dir ci-dist
      - name: Base install imports and runs
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          wheel=$(find ci-dist -maxdepth 1 -name '*.whl' -print -quit)
          uv venv --python 3.12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-base"
          uv pip install --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-base/bin/python" "$wheel"
          uv pip check --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-base/bin/python"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-base/bin/mm" --version
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-base/bin/python" tools/plugin_status_smoke.py --profile base
      - name: ONNX-only install supports E5 MCP status
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          wheel=$(find ci-dist -maxdepth 1 -name '*.whl' -print -quit)
          uv venv --python 3.12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-onnx"
          uv pip install --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-onnx/bin/python" "${wheel}[onnx]"
          uv pip check --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-onnx/bin/python"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-onnx/bin/python" tools/plugin_status_smoke.py --profile onnx
      - name: All-extras install imports
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          wheel=$(find ci-dist -maxdepth 1 -name '*.whl' -print -quit)
          uv venv --python 3.12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-all"
          uv pip install --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-all/bin/python" "${wheel}[all]"
          uv pip check --python "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-all/bin/python"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-all/bin/python" tools/extras_import_smoke.py
      # Its own out-dir, so the core steps above keep finding exactly one wheel.
      - name: Build langchain-memtomem wheel and sdist
        run: uv build packages/langchain-memtomem --out-dir ci-dist-langchain
      - name: Validate langchain-memtomem artifacts
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' packages/langchain-memtomem/pyproject.toml)
          uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python tools/release_preflight.py langchain-artifacts \
            --dist ci-dist-langchain --version "$version" --repo-root .
      # The checkout's core wheel, not a PyPI release: the floor is not on
      # PyPI before its release, and this is the core the package must work with.
      - name: langchain-memtomem installs beside the checkout's core and works
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          core=(ci-dist/memtomem-*.whl)
          langchain=(ci-dist-langchain/langchain_memtomem-*.whl)
          test "${#core[@]}" -eq 1
          test "${#langchain[@]}" -eq 1
          expect_core=$(sed -n 's/^version = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' packages/memtomem/pyproject.toml)
          test -n "$expect_core"
          uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python tools/langchain_smoke.py install \
            --artifact "${langchain[0]}" --core "${core[0]}" \
            --venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-langchain" --expect-core "$expect_core"

  vendored-assets:
    name: vendored-assets (OSV blocking)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      - run: uv sync --frozen
      # The Web UI ships SHA-pinned browser libs (DOMPurify, marked, Prism,
      # Swagger UI) that live in no package.json, so `npm audit` never sees
      # them. This queries OSV for every npm package/version in
      # web/static/vendor/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md and fails on any advisory.
      # (The SHA<->disk pin check runs offline in the `test` job.)
      - run: uv run python tools/check_vendored_advisories.py

  python-deps:
    name: python-deps (OSV blocking — Python + JavaScript)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Both shipped Python resolution metadata and the JavaScript lockfiles are
    # blocking. A reviewed exception must use the canonical owner/reason/
    # expiry schema; CI converts it to OSV Scanner's stricter native schema.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      # Hand-maintained pin: Dependabot sees no release-asset URL, so on a bump
      # update OSV_VERSION and the matching osv-scanner_linux_amd64 SHA-256 from
      # the release's osv-scanner_SHA256SUMS together.
      - name: Install osv-scanner (pinned + SHA-256 verified)
        env:
          OSV_VERSION: v2.3.8
          OSV_SHA256: bc98e15319ed0d515e3f9235287ba53cdc5535d576d24fd573978ecfe9ab92dc
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -o osv-scanner \
            "https://github.com/google/osv-scanner/releases/download/${OSV_VERSION}/osv-scanner_linux_amd64"
          echo "${OSV_SHA256}  osv-scanner" | sha256sum -c -
          chmod +x osv-scanner
      - name: Validate reviewed OSV exceptions
        run: >-
          uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python tools/check_osv_exceptions.py
          --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/osv-scanner.toml"
      # osv-scanner queries OSV.dev live, so the pinned binary never goes stale
      # on advisory data. Scan both lockfiles in one invocation so an exception
      # cannot accidentally make only one ecosystem blocking.
      - name: OSV scan (Python + JavaScript lockfiles — blocking)
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          rc=0
          ./osv-scanner scan source \
            --config="$RUNNER_TEMP/osv-scanner.toml" \
            --lockfile=uv.lock \
            --lockfile=packages/memtomem/tests-js/package-lock.json \
            --lockfile=packages/opencode-memtomem/package-lock.json \
            --format markdown --verbosity error | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || rc=$?
          # rc 0 = clean, 1 = advisories found. Higher
          # means the scan itself errored (e.g. OSV.dev unreachable), so the
          # short/empty summary must NOT be read as "clean".
          if [ "$rc" -gt 1 ]; then
            echo "> :warning: osv-scanner exited ${rc} — the advisory scan may not have completed." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  bandit:
    name: bandit (security lint — blocking)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          version: ${{ env.UV_VERSION }}
      # Bandit compares against a committed baseline and blocks only *new*
      # findings. Scoped to shipped source (src/). Regenerate the
      # baseline after an intentional change with:
      #   uvx bandit@1.9.4 -r packages/memtomem/src -f json -o tools/bandit-baseline.json
      # (A no-op regen only rewrites the generated_at timestamp — that diff is benign.)
      - name: bandit (new findings vs baseline — blocking)
        run: >-
          uvx bandit@1.9.4 -r packages/memtomem/src
          -b tools/bandit-baseline.json -q

  security-gates:
    name: security-gates
    if: ${{ always() }}
    needs: [test-js, test-opencode-plugin, vendored-assets, python-deps, bandit]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Require every security dependency to succeed
        env:
          JS_RESULT: ${{ needs.test-js.result }}
          OPENCODE_RESULT: ${{ needs.test-opencode-plugin.result }}
          VENDORED_RESULT: ${{ needs.vendored-assets.result }}
          OSV_RESULT: ${{ needs.python-deps.result }}
          BANDIT_RESULT: ${{ needs.bandit.result }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for result in "$JS_RESULT" "$OPENCODE_RESULT" "$VENDORED_RESULT" "$OSV_RESULT" "$BANDIT_RESULT"; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "security dependency did not succeed: $result" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

# memtomem > Local-first long-term memory for AI coding agents: Markdown files you own, found again with hybrid keyword + semantic search. Core usage is hook-free by default: memory changes happen only when you or your agent call memtomem. [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/memtomem)](https://pypi.org/project/memtomem/) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/memtomem)](https://pypi.org/project/memtomem/) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/memtomem/memtomem)](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem/stargazers) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue)](LICENSE) > 🧪 **Beta** — the nine core MCP tools, the `mm` CLI, and the format of your memory and config files change only with an `Upgrading` note in the [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md). Features marked **experimental** can change without one; see [Stability](#stability). Feedback is welcome: [Issues](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem/issues) · [Discussions](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem/discussions). ## The session loop Three plugin workflows carry a project's memory from one session to the next, and from one coding agent to another.

Illustrative output — agent wording and results vary. ```text # End of a session, in Claude Code > /memtomem:handoff save codex-cli handoff_id: 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c2f-1d5e6a7b8c9d scope: project_local · namespace: shared:retry-policy · 1 file written, 2 chunks indexed # Next session, in Codex CLI > $memtomem-brief Recent updates and active handoff IDs - 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c2f-1d5e6a7b8c9d from claude-code → codex-cli load it with: $memtomem-handoff resume 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c2f-1d5e6a7b8c9d > $memtomem-handoff resume 3f2a9c1e-7b4d-4e8a-9c2f-1d5e6a7b8c9d git_head matches the live HEAD · worktree clean · in sync with `origin` `refs/heads/main` # After a few commits, back in Claude Code > /memtomem:update mode: incremental · 4 of the latest 10 commits not yet reviewed saved 2 items · commit-derived: 1 · session-derived: 1 ``` `handoff save` writes one Markdown record into the project's own `.memtomem/memories.local`; `brief` only reads; `update` saves decisions, bug fixes, and preferences as separate items. All three run only when you invoke them, and nothing runs in the background. The [Project workflows](docs/guides/project-workflows.md) guide has each one's modes, checks, and host-specific names. ## Why memtomem? - **Your files stay yours.** Memories are plain `.md` files you can read, edit, and version. The search index is rebuilt from them, day-file namespaces included; tag edits and working state live only in the database ([what a rebuild restores](docs/guides/reference.md#what-a-rebuild-restores)). - **Explicit by default.** Memory operations run on your CLI or MCP calls (`mm add`, `mem_add`, `mem_index`). Optional client hooks are separate, removable integrations, not a hidden runtime default. - **One store, many tools.** Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kimi Code, and Antigravity share one local store, and any MCP client can search it. Hermes Agent joins the same store through its [plugin and memory provider](#agent-frameworks), and LangGraph apps get the same search pipeline over a store of their own with [`langchain-memtomem`](packages/langchain-memtomem/). [memtomem-stm](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm) is a separate, optional proxy that surfaces memories proactively. ## Private by design The memtomem server runs on your machine, and its database and Markdown files stay there. With the defaults (BM25-only search, no LLM, no reranker) the server sends none of your note text anywhere. Some optional providers send text to an outside service, and each one is off until you configure it; a request to a loopback address can still leave your machine if your environment routes HTTP through a proxy or the local server forwards the request to a hosted model. Separately, the MCP tools return note text to the AI client that called them, and memtomem does not control what that client sends to its own model provider. [What leaves your machine](docs/guides/configuration.md#what-leaves-your-machine) lists what each setting sends, when, and where. ## Set it up from your coding agent Paste a prompt into Claude Code, Codex CLI, or another coding agent. The agent runs the [Quick Start](#quick-start) commands for you, asks before the choices that are yours, and shows you the result. **Install and verify:** ```text Install memtomem on this computer by following https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem#quick-start. If a ~/.memtomem folder already exists, memtomem is already set up here: stop and tell me, and change nothing. Otherwise ask me which preset to use (minimal, english, or korean) and which folder should hold my memories, then run `uv tool install --python 3.12 'memtomem[all]'` and `mm init --non-interactive --preset --memory-dir --mcp skip`. Verify with `mm add "memtomem setup check" --file setup-check.md` (pick another file name if that one exists) and a `mm search` that finds it, and show me both outputs. If a command fails, stop and show me the error instead of working around it. Do not edit, move, or delete my existing notes, and do not install any hooks. Finish by telling me which plugin under "Works with" connects this agent. ``` **Something looks wrong:** ```text Check my memtomem setup with read-only commands: run `mm doctor` and `mm memory doctor`, then list each finding with the command that would fix it. Ask me before you run any fix. ``` Prefer to run the commands yourself? The Quick Start below is the same path, step by step. ## Quick Start ### 1. Install ```bash uv tool install --python 3.12 'memtomem[all]' # or: pipx install 'memtomem[all]' mm --version # verify install ``` `--python 3.12` has uv download Python 3.12 when none is installed; without it, uv can pick an older system Python and stop with `No solution found`. `[all]` bundles ONNX dense embeddings, the Korean tokenizer, the code chunker, and the Web UI (about 340 MB installed, before any model download). The Ollama and OpenAI embedding providers need no extra. A smaller install is under [Other install options](#minimal-install) below. ### 2. Setup ```bash mm init # preset picker, then memory_dir + MCP ``` The interactive picker starts with three presets — **Minimal** (BM25, no downloads), **English (Recommended)** (ONNX `multilingual-e5-small` + auto-discover providers), **Korean-optimized** (ONNX `multilingual-e5-small` + `kiwipiepy` tokenizer); no preset turns on a reranker — plus an **Advanced** entry that opens the full 10-step wizard. Preset paths only ask about the memory directory and MCP registration; everything else is set from the preset. Choose **Minimal** for the fastest no-download first proof and rerun `mm init` later to add semantic search. For automation, `mm init --non-interactive` picks the minimal preset without prompts. See [Embeddings](docs/guides/embeddings.md) for the model and provider matrix. The presets keep embedding on your machine; choosing OpenAI embeddings, a cloud LLM, or the Cohere reranker sends note text to that service ([What leaves your machine](docs/guides/configuration.md#what-leaves-your-machine)). ### 3. Verify a complete memory round trip ```bash mm status mm add "Deployment checklist uses blue-green rollout" --tags ops mm search "blue-green" ``` The last command should return the sentence you just added. `mm add` writes to your user memory directory and indexes the entry immediately, so this works without an existing notes directory or a connected editor. To bring existing notes into the same index, run `mm index /path/to/your/notes`. ### 4. Connect your coding agent Install the plugin for your tool — [Claude Code](packages/memtomem-claude-plugin/), [Codex CLI](plugins/memtomem/), [OpenCode](packages/opencode-memtomem/), [Kimi Code](packages/memtomem-kimi-skills/), [Antigravity](packages/memtomem-antigravity-plugin/), or [Cursor](packages/memtomem-cursor-plugin/) — then, in the project you work on, register the memory tier the session loop writes to: ```bash cd && mm mem init --scope project_local ``` Start a new session and run the brief workflow: `/memtomem:brief` in Claude Code, and the name each other host uses is in the [Project workflows](docs/guides/project-workflows.md) guide. The [Claude Code & Codex CLI plugin quickstart](docs/guides/plugin-quickstart.md) ([한국어](docs/guides/vibe-coding-getting-started-ko.md)) walks through plugin installation and a first memory save-and-search round trip in 10–15 minutes. For Windsurf, Claude Desktop, Gemini CLI, other MCP clients, and registering Cursor by hand instead of through the plugin, see [MCP Client Setup](docs/guides/mcp-clients.md); from any client, asking it to call the `mem_status` tool confirms the connection. ### 5. Open the Web UI (optional) ```bash mm web # dashboard on http://127.0.0.1:8080 mm web -b # run in the background; logs go to ~/.memtomem/logs/web.log mm web stop # stop the tracked Web UI process ``` `mm web` shows the polished page set. `mm web --dev` (or `MEMTOMEM_WEB__MODE=dev`) adds maintainer pages such as Sessions, Working Memory, and Health Report.
Other install options **Minimal** (no bundled model, about 50 MB): ```bash uv tool install --python 3.12 memtomem # no extras — no local ONNX model, Web UI or Korean tokenizer until you add them; Ollama/OpenAI embeddings still work ``` Opt in later per feature: `uv tool install --reinstall 'memtomem[onnx,web]'` (see the [extras table](docs/guides/getting-started.md#optional-extras)). List every extra you want to keep, because `--reinstall` replaces the whole set. A plain `mm upgrade` keeps the extras it detects from the current install, but an explicit `mm upgrade --extras` list must name the complete set too. **Project-scoped** (per-project isolation): ```bash uv add 'memtomem[all]' && uv run mm init # all commands need `uv run` prefix ``` **No install** (uvx on demand): ```bash claude mcp add memtomem -s user -e MEMTOMEM_EXTRA_TOOLS=mem_update_coverage -- uvx --python 3.12 --isolated --from "memtomem[all]==0.7.12" memtomem-server ```
Troubleshooting the install - **`mm --version` shows an older version than the [latest release](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem/releases)** right after installing: `uv` is likely serving cached PyPI metadata. Re-run with `uv tool install 'memtomem[all]' --refresh`, or clear the cache first with `uv cache clean memtomem`. To upgrade an existing uv tool install, use `mm upgrade` rather than re-running `uv tool install`; see the [CLI reference](docs/guides/reference/data-config-cli.md#cli-reference) for what it preserves and stops. - **`mm: command not found`**: `uv tool install` drops the shim into `~/.local/bin`, which is not on `$PATH` in fresh shells on macOS/Linux. Run `uv tool update-shell`, then open a new shell and re-run `mm --version`. - **Duplicate tools after upgrading the Claude plugin**: re-check `/mcp` after reloading. The plugin launches `memtomem[onnx]==0.7.12`. A manual registration whose launch differs — base-only `memtomem`, or the ONNX launch pinned to an earlier release — no longer matches for deduplication. Confirm the manual entry's name and scope, then align its launch command with the plugin or remove the redundant registration. - **Indexing vs. discovery (Claude Code)**: provider memory folders that setup auto-discovers (such as `~/.claude/projects/*/memory/`) are added to the search *index*. That is separate from the Web UI's opt-in Context Gateway scan of `~/.claude/projects/`, which discovers project *roots* for Skills, Commands, and Subagents; see [Configuration → Context Gateway](docs/guides/configuration.md#context-gateway).
## Works with Everything here runs on the [**memtomem**](https://pypi.org/project/memtomem/) core package: the MCP server, CLI, Web UI, hybrid search, and storage. [**memtomem-stm**](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm) is a separate, optional STM proxy that surfaces memories proactively by intercepting tool calls. | Use it from | For | Start here | core tools | [MCP Client Setup](docs/guides/mcp-clients.md) | | **The terminal** | Indexing, health checks, scripts (`--json` output) | [CLI chunk-level SHA-256 diff, so only changed chunks are re-embedded | [Scheduled jobs](docs/guides/reference/automation.md) for compaction, decay, dead-link cleanup, and dedup scans | LangGraph `MemtomemBaseStore`, plus the [Hybrid Store](docs/guides/langgraph-hybrid-store.md) with SQLite persistence and BM25/dense/RRF retrieval; [`langchain-memtomem`](packages/langchain-memtomem/) runs memtomem's search pipeline as a LangGraph store | | | [Scriptable CLI](docs/guides/reference/data-config-cli.md#cli-reference): `--json` output on status, search, recall, and the write commands; `mm warmup` pre-loads local models | [memtomem-stm](https://github.com/memtomem/memtomem-stm): optional proxy for proactive surfacing, compression, and caching | ## Stability memtomem is beta (`0.x`). # Git Workflow Skill

Expert patterns for Git version control workflows including branching strategies, commit conventions, collaborative workflows, and CI/CD integration.

## 🔌 Compatibility

This is an **Agent Skill** following the [open standard](https://agentskills.io) originally developed by Anthropic and released for cross-platform use.

**Supported Platforms:**
- ✅ Claude Code (Anthropic)
- ✅ Cursor
- ✅ GitHub Copilot
- ✅ Other skills-compatible AI agents

> Skills are portable packages of procedural knowledge that work across any AI agent supporting the Agent Skills specification.


## Features

- **Branching Strategies**: Git Flow (feature/release/hotfix branches), GitHub Flow (simple feature branches), trunk-based development, release management patterns
- **Commit Conventions**: Conventional Commits standard, semantic versioning integration, commit message best practices, atomic commit patterns
- **Collaborative Workflows**: Pull request best practices, code review processes, merge strategies (merge, squash, rebase), conflict resolution patterns
- **CI/CD Integration**: GitHub Actions workflows, GitLab CI patterns, branch protection rules, automated versioning
- **Git Hooks**: Pre-commit hooks for linting and testing, commit message validation
- **Advanced Operations**: Interactive rebase, cherry-picking, stashing, reflog recovery

## Installation

### Marketplace (Recommended)

Add the [Netresearch marketplace](https://github.com/netresearch/claude-code-marketplace) once, then browse and install skills:

```bash
# Claude Code
/plugin marketplace add netresearch/claude-code-marketplace
/plugin install git-workflow@netresearch-claude-code-marketplace
```

### Without a marketplace

Since Claude Code 2.1.157 a plugin directory under your personal skills directory loads on its own, including the hooks and commands this repo ships:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
git clone https://github.com/netresearch/git-workflow-skill.git \
  ~/.claude/skills/git-workflow
```

It loads as `git-workflow@skills-dir` on the next session. Update with `git -C ~/.claude/skills/git-workflow pull` and start a new session; remove it by deleting the directory. This route has no `claude plugin update`.

### npx ([skills.sh](https://skills.sh))

Install with any [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io)-compatible agent:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/netresearch/git-workflow-skill --skill git-workflow
```

> **Limitation:** `npx skills` installs `SKILL.md`-based skills only. This repo also ships `hooks`, `commands`, which it does not install — use the marketplace or the skills directory for those.

### Download Release

Download the [latest release](https://github.com/netresearch/git-workflow-skill/releases/latest) and extract to your agent's skills directory.

### Git Clone

```bash
git clone https://github.com/netresearch/git-workflow-skill.git
```

### Composer (PHP Projects)

```bash
composer require netresearch/git-workflow-skill
```

Requires [netresearch/composer-agent-skill-plugin](https://github.com/netresearch/composer-agent-skill-plugin).

### npm (Node Projects)

```bash
npm install --save-dev \
  @netresearch/agent-skill-coordinator \
  github:netresearch/git-workflow-skill
```

Requires [@netresearch/agent-skill-coordinator](https://github.com/netresearch/node-agent-skill-coordinator), which discovers the skill in `node_modules` and registers it in `AGENTS.md` via a `postinstall` hook. For pnpm, also allowlist the coordinator's postinstall:

```json
{
  "pnpm": {
    "onlyBuiltDependencies": ["@netresearch/agent-skill-coordinator"]
  }
}
```

## Usage

This skill is automatically triggered when:

- Establishing branching strategies (Git Flow, GitHub Flow, Trunk-based)
- Implementing Conventional Commits for semantic versioning
- Configuring pull request workflows
- Integrating Git with CI/CD systems
- Setting up Git hooks for quality gates
- Resolving merge conflicts
- Configuring branch protection rules

Example queries:
- "Set up Git Flow workflow"
- "Configure conventional commits with semantic versioning"
- "Create GitHub Actions workflow for CI/CD"
- "Set up pre-commit hooks for linting"
- "Configure branch protection rules"
- "Implement pull request review process"

### Commands

- `/pr-finish [PR]` — drive a pull request to a fully-green, merged state:
  preflight the merge gate in one block, rebase, fix CI locally, reply to and
  resolve every review thread, update the title/description, and merge when
  green. Operates on the named PR or the current branch's PR.

## Structure

```
git-workflow-skill/                       # abbreviated — key files only
├── skills/git-workflow/
│   ├── SKILL.md                          # Skill metadata and core patterns
│   ├── ...                               # checkpoints.yaml, evals/, hooks
│   └── references/
│       ├── commit-conventions.md         # Commit message standards
│       ├── pull-request-workflow.md      # PR and review processes
│       ├── ci-cd-integration.md          # CI watching, git mirrors
│       └── advanced-git.md               # Advanced Git operations
├── commands/
│   └── pr-finish.md                      # /pr-finish slash command
└── scripts/
    └── verify-harness.sh                 # Harness verification script
```

## Expertise Areas

### Commit Conventions
- Conventional Commits standard
- Semantic versioning mapping (`feat`/`fix`/etc.)
- Signed commits + DCO sign-off
- Atomic commit patterns

### Collaborative Workflows
- Default-branch check before PR/scripting operations
- Atomic commits, no squash unless asked
- Merge strategies, review-thread resolution, merge gate
- Conflict resolution patterns

### CI/CD Integration
- Watching CI from the CLI (`gh pr checks`, `gh run watch`)
- Git mirror repository sync (`git push --mirror` gotchas)

## Conventional Commits Format

```
<type>[optional scope]: <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer(s)]
```

**Types:**
- `feat`: New feature (MINOR version bump)
- `fix`: Bug fix (PATCH version bump)
- `docs`: Documentation only
- `style`: Code style (formatting, no logic change)
- `refactor`: Code refactoring
- `perf`: Performance improvements
- `test`: Adding/updating tests
- `build`: Build system changes
- `ci`: CI configuration changes
- `chore`: Maintenance tasks
- `revert`: Reverting changes

**Breaking Changes:**
```
feat!: remove deprecated API endpoints

BREAKING CHANGE: The /api/v1/users endpoint has been removed.
Use /api/v2/users instead.
```

## Quick Reference

### Daily Workflow

```bash
# Start of day
git checkout main && git pull
git checkout -b feature/my-feature

# During development
git add -p                    # Stage hunks interactively
git commit -m "feat: ..."     # Commit with conventional message

# Ready for review
git push -u origin HEAD
gh pr create

# After merge
git checkout main && git pull
git branch -d feature/my-feature
```

### Emergency Fixes

```bash
# Undo last commit (keep changes)
git reset --soft HEAD~1

# Undo last commit (discard changes)
git reset --hard HEAD~1

# Revert a specific commit
git revert <commit-hash>

# Fix last commit message
git commit --amend -m "new message"

# Fix last commit (add forgotten file)
git add forgotten-file.txt
git commit --amend --no-edit
```

## Related Skills

- **enterprise-readiness-skill**: Git workflow is part of CI/CD maturity
- **security-audit-skill**: Git hooks for security checks

## Governance and policies

This repository follows the organisation-wide policies of Netresearch:

- [Governance](https://github.com/netresearch/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md): roles, how changes are decided and how disputes are settled.
- [Roadmap](https://github.com/netresearch/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): planned and excluded work for the coming year.
- [Handling of dependency and code analysis findings](https://github.com/netresearch/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#handling-of-dependency-and-code-analysis-findings): which findings block a pull request, remediation times and how exceptions are recorded.
- [Secret management](https://github.com/netresearch/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secret-management): where CI and release secrets are stored, who can access them and when they are rotated.
- [Access roster](https://github.com/netresearch/.github/blob/main/docs/access-roster.md): the accounts that hold admin, maintain and write access to this repository.

What this repository does to be secure, and what it does not promise, is set out in the [security assurance case](docs/SECURITY-ASSURANCE.md).

Checks that run on pull requests in this repository:

- On every pull request: Skill Validation (`lint.yml`), Eval Validation (`eval-validate.yml`), Skill Tests (`tests.yml`) and Hook Script Tests (`hook-tests.yml`).
- On pull requests to `main`, additionally: CodeQL for GitHub Actions and Python with the `security-and-quality` queries, Betterleaks secret scanning, zizmor workflow analysis, dependency review (fails on high or critical vulnerabilities), Composer Audit and Opengrep SAST (failure threshold: [organisation SAST rule](https://github.com/netresearch/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#static-analysis-sast)), all from `security.yml`; Harness Verification (`harness-verify.yml`) and Template Drift (`check-template-drift.yml`).

## License

This project uses split licensing:

- **Code** (scripts, workflows, configs): [MIT](LICENSE-MIT)
- **Content** (skill definitions, documentation, references): [CC-BY-SA-4.0](LICENSE-CC-BY-SA-4.0)

See the individual license files for full terms.
## Credits

Developed and maintained by [Netresearch DTT GmbH](https://www.netresearch.de/).

# Hermes Agent ☤

Hermes Agent | Hermes Desktop

**The self-improving AI agent built by [Nous Research](https://nousresearch.com).** It's the only agent with a built-in learning loop — it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, searches its own past conversations, and builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure that costs nearly nothing when idle. It's not tied to your laptop — talk to it from Telegram while it works on a cloud VM. Use any model you want — [Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com), OpenRouter, OpenAI, your own endpoint, and [many others](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/integrations/providers). Switch with `hermes model` — no code changes, no lock-in.
A real terminal interfaceFull TUI with multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, conversation history, interrupt-and-redirect, and streaming tool output.
Lives where you doTelegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI — all from a single gateway process. Voice memo transcription, cross-platform conversation continuity.
A closed learning loopAgent-curated memory with periodic nudges. Autonomous skill creation after complex tasks. Skills self-improve during use. FTS5 session search with LLM summarization for cross-session recall. Honcho dialectic user modeling. Compatible with the agentskills.io open standard.
Scheduled automationsBuilt-in cron scheduler with delivery to any platform. Daily reports, nightly backups, weekly audits — all in natural language, running unattended.

Write Python scripts that call tools via RPC, collapsing multi-step pipelines into zero-context-cost turns.

Daytona and Modal offer serverless persistence — your agent's environment hibernates when idle and wakes on demand, costing nearly nothing between sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS or a GPU cluster.

--- ## Quick Install ### Linux, macOS, WSL2 ```bash curl -fsSL https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh | bash ``` ### Windows (native, PowerShell) > **Heads up:** Native Windows runs Hermes without WSL — CLI, gateway, TUI, and tools all work natively. If you'd rather use WSL2, the Linux/macOS one-liner above works there too. Found a bug? Please [file issues](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues). Run this in PowerShell: ```powershell iex (irm https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.ps1) ``` The source installer delegates Python 3.14, Node.js, npm, pnpm, ripgrep, FFmpeg, and Python dependencies to PM. If Git is absent, it stages the verified Git for Windows archive in Hermes' tool store. It does not replace your system Git. See [installation methods](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/installation) for the separate MSIX/App Installer package and its update ownership. > **Android / Termux:** A signed APT repository is available for aarch64 devices, with a `stable` channel (tagged releases) and a prerelease `canary` channel. The package includes Python, Node.js, and the TUI. Use the [Termux guide](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/getting-started/termux), not the desktop/server installer script. > > **Windows:** Native Windows is fully supported — the PowerShell one-liner above installs everything. If you'd rather use WSL2, the Linux command works there too. Native Windows install lives under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`; WSL2 installs under `~/.hermes` as on Linux. After installation: ```bash source ~/.bashrc # reload shell (or: source ~/.zshrc) hermes # start chatting! ``` ### Troubleshooting #### Windows Defender or antivirus flags `uv.exe` as malware If your antivirus (Bitdefender, Windows Defender, etc.) quarantines `uv.exe` from the Hermes `bin` folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\bin\uv.exe`), this is a **false positive**. The file is Astral's `uv` — the Rust Python package manager Hermes bundles to manage its Python environment. ML-based antivirus engines commonly flag unsigned Rust binaries that download and install packages. **To verify your copy is authentic:** ```powershell # Install GitHub CLI if needed winget install --id GitHub.cli # Login to GitHub gh auth login # Run verification $uv = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin\uv.exe" $ver = (& $uv --version).Split(' ')[1] [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12 $zip = "$env:TEMP\uv.zip" Invoke-WebRequest "https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/download/$ver/uv-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip" -OutFile $zip -UseBasicParsing gh attestation verify $zip --repo astral-sh/uv Expand-Archive $zip "$env:TEMP\uv_x" -Force (Get-FileHash "$env:TEMP\uv_x\uv.exe").Hash -eq (Get-FileHash $uv).Hash ``` If attestation says "Verification succeeded" and the last line prints `True`, you're good. **To whitelist Hermes:** - **Windows Defender:** Run PowerShell as Admin → `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\hermes\bin"` - **Bitdefender:** Add an exception in the Bitdefender console (Protection > Antivirus > Settings > Manage Exceptions) - Whitelist the **folder**, not the file hash — Hermes updates `uv` and the hash changes every version For more context, see the upstream Astral reports: [astral-sh/uv#13553](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/13553), [astral-sh/uv#15011](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/15011), [astral-sh/uv#10079](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/10079). --- ## Getting Started ```bash hermes # Interactive CLI — start a conversation hermes model # Choose your LLM provider and model hermes tools # Configure which tools are enabled hermes config set # Set individual config values hermes config get # Print individual config values hermes gateway # Start the messaging gateway (Telegram, Discord, etc.) hermes setup # Run the full setup wizard (configures everything at once) hermes update # Update to the latest version hermes doctor # Diagnose any issues ``` 📖 **[Full documentation →](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/)** --- ## Skip the API-key collection — Nous Portal Hermes works with whatever provider you want — that's not changing. But if you'd rather not collect five separate API keys for the model, web search, image generation, TTS, and a cloud browser, **[Nous Portal](https://portal.nousresearch.com)** covers all of them under one subscription: - **300+ models** — pick any of them with `/model ` - **Tool Gateway** — web search, image generation (FAL), text-to-speech (OpenAI), cloud browser (Browser Use), all routed through your sub. No extra accounts. One command from a fresh install: ```bash hermes setup --portal ``` That logs you in via OAuth, sets Nous as your provider, and turns on the Tool Gateway. Check what's wired up any time with `hermes portal info`. Full details on the [Tool Gateway docs page](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tool-gateway). You can still bring your own keys per-tool whenever you want — the gateway is per-backend, not all-or-nothing. --- ## CLI vs Messaging Quick Reference Hermes has two entry points: start the terminal UI with `hermes`, or run the gateway and talk to it from Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, or Email. Once you're in a conversation, many slash commands are shared across both interfaces. | Action | CLI | Messaging platforms | | ------------------------------ | personality | `/personality [name]` | `/personality [name]` | | Retry or undo the last turn | `/retry`, `/undo` | `/retry`, `/undo` | | Compress context / check usage | `/compress`, `/usage`,
