# renovate-mcp

[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/renovate-mcp.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/renovate-mcp)
[![CI](https://github.com/tibuntu/renovate-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tibuntu/renovate-mcp/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Node ≥ 24](https://img.shields.io/node/v/renovate-mcp.svg)](https://nodejs.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](./LICENSE)

An MCP server for designing [Renovate](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate) configurations interactively. Point it at a local repo and let an LLM help you read, validate, preview, and save `renovate.json`.

## Quick start

Needs Node.js ≥ 24.11 on Linux or macOS. With [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code):

```bash
npm install -g renovate-mcp
claude mcp add renovate -s user -- renovate-mcp
claude mcp list   # renovate should show as connected
```

Then try the prompt: *"List the namespaces available under `renovate://presets`."* A response listing `config`, `docker`, `npm`, … confirms the server is reachable. No tokens are needed for the offline tools. Other clients, tokens and upgrades are under [Install](#install) below.

## What you can do

- **Read and explain configs** — locate the active `renovate.json*`, expand every `extends` preset offline, and trace which preset set each field.
- **Discover presets from intent** — describe what you want ("automerge patches, group dev deps") and get ranked built-in (and your own local-repo) presets, plus a draft config skeleton when nothing fits.
- **Preview custom managers** before running Renovate — regex and JSONata, with Renovate's `managerFilePatterns` glob/regex file selection, file/line hits and extracted dep info.
- **Validate and lint** — schema validation plus a semantic lint pass for Renovate-specific footguns (unwrapped regexes, unknown manager names, deprecated keys).
- **Dry-run** against a local checkout or a remote GitHub/GitLab — see exactly which PRs Renovate would open.
- **Save back atomically** — round-trip writes preserve comments and key order in existing JSON-with-comments files.

## Tools & resources

Nineteen tools, seven resources, and five workflow prompts. Each tool name below links to its full reference in [`docs/tools.md`](docs/tools.md).

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| [`check_setup`](docs/tools.md#check_setup) | Report Renovate CLI + validator availability, versions, install hints, and a `platformContext` block for env diagnosis. Also runs at startup. Pass an optional `repoPath` to add a `repoContext` block diagnosing the repo's git origin, config endpoint/platform, endpoint reachability, and token coverage. |
| [`get_version`](docs/tools.md#get_version) | Report the renovate-mcp server version and whether it's a released or local/dev build. |
| [`read_config`](docs/tools.md#read_config) | Locate and parse a repo's Renovate config in Renovate's own discovery order. |
| [`suggest_presets`](docs/tools.md#suggest_presets) | Search built-in (and optional local-repo) presets by natural-language intent; ranks matches and sketches an unvalidated draft config skeleton for multi-facet or weakly-covered intents. Offline. |
| [`resolve_config`](docs/tools.md#resolve_config) | Expand every `extends` preset offline. Opt in to fetching `github>` / `gitlab>` / `gitea>` / `forgejo>` presets over HTTPS, or Bitbucket Cloud presets via `local>` + `platform`. |
| [`explain_config`](docs/tools.md#explain_config) | Inverse of `resolve_config`: annotate every leaf field with the chain of presets that set it. |
| [`resolve_config_diff`](docs/tools.md#resolve_config_diff) | Offline structural diff of two fully-resolved configs — changed fields plus an order-insensitive set diff of array keys (`packageRules`, `customManagers`, …). The refactor-friendly counterpart to `dry_run_diff`. |
| [`test_package_rules`](docs/tools.md#test_package_rules) | Offline what-if: which `packageRules` match a hypothetical dependency, which matcher decided each, and what each contributes — plus the `branchName` / `commitMessage` / `prTitle` the matched config would render for it. Faithful matching (Renovate's real matchers in a worker); fields you don't supply are reported as unevaluatable, not non-matches, and the rendered names list the post-lookup template variables they could not fill. |
| [`preview_custom_manager`](docs/tools.md#preview_custom_manager) | Preview a `customManagers` entry (regex or JSONata) against a local repo. Offline. |
| [`validate_config`](docs/tools.md#validate_config) | Run `renovate-config-validator` against a file or inline object. |
| [`lint_config`](docs/tools.md#lint_config) | Semantic lint pass for Renovate-specific footguns the schema validator declares valid. Offline. |
| [`dry_run`](docs/tools.md#dry_run) | Run Renovate with `--dry-run` and return the structured JSON report. Local-by-default, flattening `local>` presets with Renovate's own resolver into a temporary copy first; a draft passed as `configContent` runs in that copy too, so it can be tested before `write_config`; remote with `platform` + `endpoint` + `token` + `repository`. No PRs, no pushes. |
| [`dry_run_diff`](docs/tools.md#dry_run_diff) | Stateless semantic diff between two `dry_run` reports — added / removed / changed updates. |
| [`annotate_dry_run`](docs/tools.md#annotate_dry_run) | Attribute each proposed update in a `dry_run` report to the `packageRules` that caused it; flags rules that never matched and report fields the matchers needed but the report lacked. Stateless + offline. |
| [`explain_dependency`](docs/tools.md#explain_dependency) | Answer "why was/wasn't dependency X updated?" from a `dry_run` report: per-occurrence `skipReason`, proposed `updates`, `warnings`, a one-line verdict and remedy hints; optionally the `packageRules` that matched it. Stateless + offline. |
| [`explain_schedule`](docs/tools.md#explain_schedule) | Answer "when will this `schedule` actually run?": active-now plus the next run windows in UTC and the config's `timezone`, computed with Renovate's own schedule matcher; invalid schedules return Renovate's message and the fact that it then runs at any time. Offline. |
| [`explain_paths`](docs/tools.md#explain_paths) | Show which files Renovate scans under `includePaths` / `ignorePaths` (preset-added ones included, each attributed to its source), flag dead patterns and `ignorePaths` entries that drop files only by substring (`test` dropping `src/latest/`), and count each `matchFileNames` entry against the real repo. Offline. |
| [`migrate_config`](docs/tools.md#migrate_config) | Apply Renovate's built-in migrations and return the migrated config plus a unified diff. Does not write. |
| [`write_config`](docs/tools.md#write_config) | Validate, then atomically write a config to disk. Preserves comments/key order on existing JSON-with-comments files; for `package.json` edits only the nested `renovate` key. |
| [`renovate://presets`](docs/tools.md#renovatepresets) (resource) | Markdown index of all built-in presets grouped by namespace. |
| [`renovate://presets/{namespace}`](docs/tools.md#renovatepresetsnamespace) (resource) | Markdown listing for a single namespace. |
| [`renovate://preset/{name}`](docs/tools.md#renovatepresetname) (resource) | Expanded JSON body for one preset. |
| [`renovate://options`](docs/tools.md#renovateoptions) (resource) | Markdown index of all Renovate config options, split into repository and global/self-hosted-only sections. |
| [`renovate://option/{name}`](docs/tools.md#renovateoptionname) (resource) | Full definition of one config option as JSON. |
| [`renovate://managers`](docs/tools.md#renovatemanagers) (resource) | Markdown list of all manager names, including custom managers. |
| [`renovate://datasources`](docs/tools.md#renovatedatasources) (resource) | Markdown list of all built-in datasource ids. |

**Prompts.** Five workflow prompts package the tool sequences above into ready-to-run starting points. Claude Code surfaces MCP prompts as slash commands (e.g. `/mcp__renovate__design-renovate-config`); other MCP clients expose them through their own prompt picker.

| Prompt | Drives |
| --- | --- |
| [`design-renovate-config`](docs/tools.md#design-renovate-config) | `check_setup` → `read_config` → `suggest_presets` → `resolve_config`/`explain_config` → `validate_config`/`lint_config` → `dry_run` of the draft (`configContent`) → `write_config` on confirmation. |
| [`debug-package-rule`](docs/tools.md#debug-package-rule) | `check_setup` → `read_config` → `test_package_rules` (matches + rendered names) → `dry_run` (with `reportOutputPath`) → `annotate_dry_run` → `explain_dependency` → a verdict naming rule indices and matchers. |
| [`author-custom-manager`](docs/tools.md#author-custom-manager) | Draft a `customManagers` entry → `preview_custom_manager` iteratively → `validate_config`/`lint_config` → `dry_run` of the draft (`configContent`) → `write_config` on confirmation. |
| [`onboard-repo`](docs/tools.md#onboard-repo) | For repos without a config: `check_setup` → `read_config` (expect none) → `dry_run` (extract mode) → `suggest_presets` → `lint_config`/`validate_config` → full `dry_run` of the draft (`configContent`) → `write_config` on confirmation. |
| [`check-config-after-upgrade`](docs/tools.md#check-config-after-upgrade) | After a Renovate bot upgrade: `check_setup` (version comparison) → `read_config` → `migrate_config`/`lint_config`/`validate_config` → `dry_run` (extract mode) → new features from release notes or `renovate://options` → `write_config` on confirmation. |

## Requirements

- **Linux or macOS.** Windows is not supported — `package.json` declares `"os": ["darwin", "linux"]`, so `npm i` surfaces an `EBADPLATFORM` warning on Windows and the server exits with a clear stderr message at startup. Use WSL2 or a Linux/macOS host instead.
- **Node.js ≥ 24.11** (aligns with Renovate's own engine requirement).

Renovate ships bundled — the `renovate` package is a runtime dependency, so `validate_config`, `dry_run`, and `write_config` work out of the box with no separate install. The offline tools (`read_config`, `suggest_presets`, `resolve_config`, `explain_config`, `resolve_config_diff`, `test_package_rules`, `preview_custom_manager`, `lint_config`, `dry_run_diff`, `annotate_dry_run`, `explain_dependency`, `explain_schedule`, `explain_paths`, `migrate_config`) never spawn Renovate at all — nor do `check_setup` (by default it reads version metadata from the bundled install instead of spawning) or `get_version` (it only reports the renovate-mcp server's own version).

**Optional env vars:**

- `RENOVATE_BIN` / `RENOVATE_CONFIG_VALIDATOR_BIN` — override the bundled binaries. When set, the override always wins.
- `RENOVATE_MCP_REQUIRE_CLI=false` — suppress the startup "partial availability" notice when you only intend to use the offline tools.
- Platform + token env vars — see [`docs/platform-setup.md`](docs/platform-setup.md) for the per-platform matrix. Preset fetching and `dry_run` bind every token to its own host; `RENOVATE_TOKEN` only covers the home host named by `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` / `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT`. A `platform` / `endpoint` passed on a call routes requests but never moves a token.
- `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` — JSON array of `{matchHost, hostType, tokenEnv}` naming the env var that holds the token for an extra host (never the value itself). See [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md#token-resolution).
- `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` — authenticates github.com *datasource* lookups (release notes, `github-tags` / `github-releases` / `github-actions`). Distinct from the platform token and never auto-derived from it; set it when github.com-hosted deps are resolved under the default `dry_run` `platform: local`. See [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md#github_com_token--a-separate-role).

> Heads up: MCP servers do **not** inherit your shell env. Set every env var via the `env` key in `.mcp.json` / `claude_desktop_config.json`. See [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md#where-env-vars-must-live).

## Install

### 1. Install the package

```bash
npm install -g renovate-mcp
```

Install before you register the server. The package bundles Renovate (about 670 packages, 350 MB), so a client that starts `npx -y renovate-mcp` against a cold npm cache downloads all of that during server startup and can time out.

Upgrade with `npm install -g renovate-mcp@latest` and restart your client. With nvm or fnm, global packages belong to one Node version — reinstall after switching.

### 2. Register it with your client

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add renovate -s user -- renovate-mcp
```

`-s user` makes the server available in every project. Leave it out to register it for the current project only, or use `-s project` to write a shared `.mcp.json`.

**Claude Desktop and other GUI clients** don't load your shell's PATH, so with nvm, fnm or Homebrew they may find no Node or an older one. Use absolute paths:

```bash
which node                                        # → "command"
echo "$(npm root -g)/renovate-mcp/dist/index.js"  # → "args"
```

Claude Desktop reads `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "renovate": {
      "command": "/Users/you/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.1/bin/node",
      "args": ["/Users/you/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.1/lib/node_modules/renovate-mcp/dist/index.js"]
    }
  }
}
```

Any other client that can launch a stdio MCP server works with the same command.

### 3. Add tokens (optional)

The offline tools need nothing. Add env vars only for what you use:

| Use case | Env vars |
| --- | --- |
| Local `dry_run` on a repo with github.com dependencies | `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` (read-only PAT, avoids anonymous rate limits) |
| `dry_run` against GitHub, or private `github>` presets | `RENOVATE_PLATFORM=github` + `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| `dry_run` against GitLab, or private `gitlab>` presets | `RENOVATE_PLATFORM=gitlab` + `GITLAB_TOKEN` |
| Private presets on another host | `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` + the variable it names |

Self-hosted GitLab and GitHub Enterprise also need `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` — see [Platform setup](#platform-setup). Each token is only sent to its own platform's host.

In Claude Code, re-register with `-e`:

```bash
claude mcp remove renovate -s user
claude mcp add renovate -s user -e GITHUB_COM_TOKEN=ghp_xxx -- renovate-mcp
```

- `-e` stores the value in plain text in `~/.claude.json`. Keep tokens in `user` or `local` scope, never in a `project`-scope `.mcp.json` that gets committed.
- `-e` accepts several values, so keep the `--` before `renovate-mcp`.
- Other clients take the same variables in an `"env": { … }` block next to `"args"`.

### Alternatives

- **npx without a global install** — register `npx -y renovate-mcp` instead, after warming the npm cache once with `npm exec --yes --package=renovate-mcp -- node -e 0`.
- **Installer script** — `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tibuntu/renovate-mcp/main/install.sh | bash` runs steps 1 and 2 interactively: it checks Node, asks for `npx` or global mode, verifies the server with an MCP `initialize` handshake, and registers it via `claude mcp add` when the Claude Code CLI is on PATH. Flags (after `bash -s --`): `--global`, `--npx`, `--no-mcp-add`, `--mcp-scope=user|project|local`, `--version=X.Y.Z`; also accepted as env vars (`RENOVATE_MCP_GLOBAL=1`, `RENOVATE_MCP_NO_MCP_ADD=1`, `RENOVATE_MCP_VERSION=…`).
- **From source** — clone, run `npm install && npm run build`, and point your client at `node /absolute/path/to/renovate-mcp/dist/index.js`.

## Platform setup

For `dry_run` against a remote platform or `resolve_config` with `externalPresets: true`:

| Setup | `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` | `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` | Token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| github.com | `github` | (omit) | `RENOVATE_TOKEN` *or* `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| GitHub Enterprise | `github` | `https://github.example.com/api/v3/` | `RENOVATE_TOKEN` *or* `GITHUB_TOKEN` |
| gitlab.com | `gitlab` | (omit) | `RENOVATE_TOKEN` *or* `GITLAB_TOKEN` |
| Self-hosted GitLab | `gitlab` | `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/` | `RENOVATE_TOKEN` *or* `GITLAB_TOKEN` |
| gitea.com / Forgejo (code.forgejo.org) | — | (omit) | `GITEA_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_TOKEN` |
| Self-hosted Gitea / Forgejo | `gitea` / `forgejo` | `https://forgejo.example.com/api/v1` | `RENOVATE_TOKEN` *or* `GITEA_TOKEN` / `FORGEJO_TOKEN` |
| Bitbucket Cloud | — | (omit) | `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` |

The Gitea / Forgejo / Bitbucket Cloud rows apply to the `resolve_config` family only: `dry_run` runs Renovate as `local` / `github` / `gitlab` and only passes those tokens on as host rules for their hosts. `platform` (`gitea` / `forgejo` / `bitbucket`) and `endpoint` can also be passed as tool inputs, but they only route `local>` presets: a token goes only to its platform's public host or to the env home (`RENOVATE_PLATFORM` at `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT`, where `RENOVATE_TOKEN` comes first), so an endpoint passed only per call needs a `RENOVATE_MCP_HOST_TOKENS` entry. `endpoint` routes `local>` presets only, as in Renovate.

See [`docs/platform-setup.md`](docs/platform-setup.md) for a worked self-hosted GitLab example, `local>` preset handling, and private-registry credentials.

## Example prompts

Once the server is wired up, try prompts like these. Written for Claude but work with any MCP-capable client.

**Understanding an existing config**

- "Read the Renovate config in this repo and summarize what it actually does — expand every preset so I can see the real effective behavior."
- "Resolve my config and list anything that landed in `presetsUnresolved`, with the reason for each."
- "Why is my `prCreation` set to `not-pending`? Use `explain_config` to trace which preset set it."

**Discovering & browsing presets**

- "I want to automerge patch and minor updates and group my dev dependencies — suggest presets for that, search my `../renovate-presets` repo too, and draft a config I can validate."
- "List the presets in the `config` namespace." (uses the `renovate://presets/config` sub-resource — cheaper than pulling the whole index)
- "What does `config:recommended` actually enable? Show me its expanded JSON."
- "Find a built-in preset that pins GitHub Actions digests." (or use `suggest_presets` with that intent)

**Self-hosted GitLab / GitHub Enterprise** (env set per [Platform setup](#platform-setup))

- "Resolve my config with external presets enabled. Its `local>platform/renovate-presets` presets live on our self-hosted GitLab at `https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4`."
- "Resolve my config with external presets enabled. Its `local>acme/renovate-config//base` preset lives on our GitHub Enterprise at `https://github.acme.corp/api/v3`."
- "Dry-run `infrastructure/kubernetes/our-platform` (a nested-group GitLab project) so Renovate can fetch the `local>` presets the config extends."

**Authoring a custom manager (regex or JSONata)**

- "I have `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=...` comments above image tags in my Dockerfiles. Draft a `customManagers` regex entry with `managerFilePatterns: ["**/Dockerfile"]` and preview it against this repo so I can see what it extracts."
- "Here's a `customManagers` entry — preview it and tell me which files match `managerFilePatterns`, which lines hit each `matchStrings` regex, and what dep info gets extracted."
- "My custom manager still uses `fileMatch`. Lint the config, then run `migrate_config` so it becomes `managerFilePatterns`."
- "Draft a `customType: \"jsonata\"` customManager with `fileFormat: \"yaml\"` to extract Helm chart dependencies (`name`, `version`, `repository`) from `Chart.yaml`, and preview it against this repo."

**Validating, previewing, saving**

- "Validate this proposed config against Renovate's schema without writing it anywhere."
- "Do a dry run and show me which PRs Renovate would open — no pushes."
- "Dry-run this draft config against the repo before we write it."
- "Why didn't Renovate update `lodash`? Run a dry run and explain that dependency."
- "Add `:semanticCommits` to my `extends`, validate it, and save back to `renovate.json`."

## Example session

A transcript-style walkthrough: design a Dockerfile custom manager from scratch, validate it, dry-run, and save. Turns are abbreviated — your client will show the actual tool-call JSON.

> **You:** I've got `# renovate: datasource=docker depName=<image>` comments above `FROM` lines in my Dockerfiles. Draft a `customManagers` entry and preview it against this repo.
>
> **Claude** calls `preview_custom_manager` with a first-draft `managerFilePatterns` (`**/Dockerfile`) + `matchStrings`.
> → 4 Dockerfiles matched `managerFilePatterns`, 0 lines matched `matchStrings`. The regex anchored on `ARG`, but the Dockerfiles use `FROM`.
>
> **You:** Rewrite `matchStrings` to anchor on the renovate comment, then `FROM <image>:<version>` on the next line.
>
> **Claude** calls `preview_custom_manager` again with the fixed regex.
> → 4 files, 4 line hits. Extracted: `postgres:15.3-alpine`, `redis:7.2`, `nginx:1.25`, `node:20.11`. Named groups `depName` and `currentValue` populated on every hit.
>
> **You:** Good. Validate the full config inline, with this `customManagers` entry alongside my existing `extends`.
>
> **Claude** calls `validate_config` with the inline config. → valid.
>
> **You:** Now dry-run that config so I can see what Renovate would actually open, before anything is saved.
>
> **Claude** calls `dry_run` with the same config as `configContent`. It runs in a temporary copy of the repo, so `renovate.json` is untouched. → `configSource: "input"`, 2 updates: `postgres` 15.3-alpine → 15.5-alpine, `redis` 7.2 → 7.4. No entries in `problems`.
>
> **You:** Save it.
>
> **Claude** calls `write_config` on `renovate.json`. → validated, written atomically; because the file already existed and parsed as JSON-with-comments, the round-trip serializer preserved the surrounding comments and key order — only the `customManagers` slice was edited in place.

## Development

```bash
npm run dev                     # build watch mode
npm run typecheck               # tsc --noEmit
npm run build                   # compile to dist/
npm start                       # run the built server over stdio
npm test                        # vitest run (builds first)
npm run test:watch              # vitest watch mode
npm run test:coverage           # vitest run --coverage
npm run generate:presets        # regenerate src/data/presets.generated.ts
npm run generate:managers       # regenerate src/data/managers.generated.ts
npm run generate:migrations     # regenerate src/data/migrations.generated.ts
npm run generate:options        # regenerate src/data/options.generated.ts
npm run generate:datasources    # regenerate src/data/datasources.generated.ts
npm run sync:jsonata-pin        # sync package.json's jsonata pin to Renovate's own
npm run check:snapshot-versions # fail if any src/data/*.generated.ts is stale vs installed renovate
```

See [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) for snapshot-file mechanics, CI matrix, the nightly upstream-drift workflow, dependency review, and integration-test setup.

## Further reading

- [`docs/tools.md`](docs/tools.md) — full per-tool reference with all inputs, outputs, and edge cases.
- [`docs/platform-setup.md`](docs/platform-setup.md) — per-platform env vars, worked example, `local>` presets, private-registry credentials.
- [`docs/security.md`](docs/security.md) — token handling, env-var precedence, endpoint allowlist, redirect/body-cap policy, inline-secrets warning.
- [`docs/operations.md`](docs/operations.md) — timeouts, caps, large-report escape hatch, `ok` semantics, RE2 / nodeEnv handling, progress notifications.
- [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — shell-out vs import, worker isolation, round-trip writer, preset catalogue.
- [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) — snapshot mechanics, CI matrix, nightly drift workflow, integration testing.

## What this is NOT

- **Not a Renovate replacement.** This server doesn't open PRs, run scheduled updates, or execute in CI — it's a design-time companion for a local `renovate.json`. Use the real Renovate for the actual dependency-update pipeline.
- **`resolve_config` merges faithfully.** Preset expansion runs offline against a committed snapshot, then folds with Renovate's real `mergeChildConfig` in a worker thread — `mergeQuality: "faithful"` (it falls back to an approximate in-process merge as `"preview"` only if the worker is unavailable). Template substitution still implements only positional `{{argN}}` placeholders — non-positional tokens and Handlebars helpers are flagged in `warnings` and pass through verbatim. For full config resolution (datasource lookups, etc.), run `dry_run`.
- **`preview_custom_manager` is a subset of Renovate's custom managers.** It covers `customType: "regex"` (with `matchStringsStrategy` of `any` / `combination` / `recursive`) and `customType: "jsonata"` (with `fileFormat: "json" | "yaml" | "toml"`). File selection follows Renovate's `managerFilePatterns` semantics (globs or `/regex/`, entries unioned like Renovate's extract phase); the deprecated `fileMatch` is still accepted with a warning. Template substitution is `{{groupName}}` only — full Handlebars helpers/conditionals are not implemented. Other custom types (e.g. `html`) are out of scope. Use it for fast iteration; confirm with `dry_run`. Full coverage matrix in [`docs/tools.md#preview_custom_manager`](docs/tools.md#preview_custom_manager).
- **`dry_run` still uses fake binaries in CI.** The bundled Renovate is available (it's a runtime dependency), and `validate_config` / `write_config` have real-validator integration tests (`test/integration/realValidator.test.ts`) exercising the actual bundled `renovate-config-validator` — but `dry_run` itself still runs per-PR against fake binaries via `RENOVATE_BIN` / `RENOVATE_CONFIG_VALIDATOR_BIN` env overrides, for determinism and speed. A separate nightly workflow re-runs the full suite against `renovate@latest` end-to-end. Run `dry_run` locally against a real config to validate behaviour.

Keep it at feature parity with iOS."* Give the Bot a goal, not a backlog. - **Bot-to-bot handoffs** — grants let a QA Bot find a bug, pull in a Developer Bot to fix it, retest on staging, and have a PM Bot report status to the channel. - **Scheduled checks** — a Bot that watches an alerts channel on a cron, owns the check, and opens fixes when it regresses (Layout Bot pattern). - **Roll-up reporting** — one supervising Bot collects every subordinate Bot's pending decisions into a single thread (SuperJennyStack pattern). - **Bots × Apps** — Bots maintain Devin Apps: build new pages/features and adapt to changes automatically; Bots and Apps pin to the same nav rail ([@dabit3](https://x.com/dabit3)). - **Living evals** — a scheduled Devin reads production traces, groups them into behaviors, replays failures in a full copy of your system (never mocks), and freezes each as an eval PR — the skill file is the asset, not the evals (Rox: 72% coverage vs 43–57%). - **Bots that tune Devin itself** — Walden's bot watches user feedback, replays prompts, runs experiments, builds eval sets, and tunes Devin's own proactivity/autonomy parameters — Bots built Bots ([thread](https://x.com/walden_yan/status/2122740852091216274)). - **Bots with their own accounts** — DevRelBot ships tutorial videos by itself because it was provisioned like an employee: own computer, own Devin/GitHub/Linear accounts, own ElevenLabs key — it signs into Devin and records the real UI. - **Inter-bot protocol (BotSpeak)** — 20+ Bots generate 700+ messages/day; Jenny solved inbox collapse with a bot-to-bot shorthand (ACK codes, Simplified English, emoji receipts) and full prose only for the human — bot-made decisions 12×'d in 6 days. - **Reference-grounded swarms** — Harvey's lesson: when work can be checked against a reliable reference (real Word behavior), a small team can direct a large swarm safely. ### Reported results **1,000+ beta testers** in the weeks before launch. Day 1: ~15 bots, honest friction (session tracking doesn't scale to a fleet — "which one produced a PR? which one needs me?"), video QA that beats screenshots, 18% of weekly quota spent on setup. [Day 2](https://www.raijuna.com/blog/devin-100-day-challenge-day-2): Bots lost context within minutes and didn't pick up tasks on a GPT model (his caveat: maybe the model), the bot/local/VPS/cloud session view stayed unreadable, 33% of the week gone — "doesn't compete with open source and what you can build on your own machines" yet. Ongoing — watch this one. - **[swyx's week with Devin Bots](https://x.com/swyx/status/2122746401482592549)** — He handed over AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin and video editing, and moved off local worktrees: "multi-agent teams done right… you don't want 'AI Employees', you want agent managers that own outcomes." Caveat he's stated himself: Cognition-affiliated, no quality metrics — a practitioner report, not a benchmark. - **[linux.do — the poke.com/bots promo, from inside](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206201)** (zh) — A 20-post community log of the free-Bot experiment's failure modes: Poke negotiates grants down ($45→$20→$5), then the backend rejects the agreed number anyway; iMessage-only eligibility learned only after registering on Android; "玩不起可以不出这个活动". The missing fine print, crowd-sourced. - **[掘金 — Devin 估值 470 亿，但我的踩坑史](https://juejin.cn/post/7680768670986092544)** (zh) — A skeptical real-user account: hand Devin a Go microservice + Redis cache task that takes 30 min by hand, and read where the autonomy leaks. Useful ballast next to the case-study numbers. - **[A solo founder's $20k/month Devin operation](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/i-spent-20000-on-devin-in-a-month)** — Ryan Carson (Untangle) runs ~15 concurrent Devin agents coordinated by a folder system + paper P0 list, not a dashboard; a "Watchdog" playbook covers customer success across every law-firm account, and a "LAN PR" skill closes ~40 PRs/day without a QA reviewer (Lenny's podcast).

The bar for inclusion is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Contents - [Devin Bots — official product](#devin-bots--official-product) — deployments, reusable patterns, results, the 16-template marketplace - [Products built with Devin](#products-built-with-devin) — shipped software where Devin wrote the code - [Enterprise deployments](#enterprise-deployments) — published customer cases with hard numbers - [Bots & surfaces](#bots--surfaces) — Devin inside Discord, Telegram, Slack and other products - [SDKs & API tooling](#sdks--api-tooling) - [Tooling around Devin](#tooling-around-devin) — what the community builds *for* Devin - [Patterns & write-ups](#patterns--write-ups) — documented real-world usage - [Community media](#community-media) - [Official resources](#official-resources) ## Devin Bots — official product Launched **November 17, 2026** ([announcement](https://devin.ai/blog/introducing-devin-bots) · [docs](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/bots) · [Fortune exclusive](https://fortune.com/2026/11/17/exclusive-cognition-bets-on-devin-bots-coding-agents-in-challenge-to-anthropics-duet-and-openais-dots/)). A Bot is a persistent agent that owns an outcome: it plans the work, runs a Devin session for each piece, keeps memory across weeks, and brings you only the decisions that need your judgment. Bots live in Slack and iMessage, run on schedules or event triggers, and hand work between each other through grants. Bots incorporate technology from the Interaction Company (Poke), which Cognition acquired in July 2026. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Outcome prompt
own this, not a ticket"] --> B[Devin Bot] B -->|spawns one per task| S[Devin sessions] S --> P[Pull requests] B <-->|accumulates| M[(Memory)] B -->|only when judgment needed| H[Needs you] H -->|your call| B B -.->|grants| B2[Other Bots] ``` ### Documented deployments | Bot | Owner | What it owns | Reported results | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Android Bot** | Cognition | Devin's Android app, end to end | Prompted *"your job is to product manage the android app"* on Sep 28, 2026 — filed its own tickets, ran a Devin session per ticket, shipped to Google Play open beta in **44 days**: 1,134 PRs merged, 344,651 lines of Kotlin, 2,841 screenshot tests. Its human sent **183 messages total** — 22 days of complete silence — and **88% of PRs were self-merged**. Now owns Android/iOS feature parity. | | **Layout Bot** | Cognition | Layout-shift regression on the Devin web app | Every 3 hours it builds production `main`, simulates first/repeat/delayed-request visits, traces regressions to the introducing PR, opens fixes with before/after videos. **159 PRs in 3 weeks; lag −70%.** | | **Super Jenny** | Jenny Xu (community) | An entire mobile game studio | ~20 Bots (dev, Unity, releases, UI, iOS, Android, device testing) under one orchestrating Bot; the only human answers a consolidated Slack thread 4×/day **with emoji**. ~50 → **1,900 PRs/week**, studio revenue 6×'d, shipping weekly. Published as community template **SuperJennyStack**. She then built **BotSpeak** — a token-saving bot-to-bot shorthand (ASD-STE100, ACK codes, emoji receipts; full prose only for the human): bot-made decisions **12×'d** in 6 days. ([Jenny's thread](https://x.com/xujennyc), [BotSpeak post](https://x.com/xujennyc/status/2123111543105868166)) | | **dabit3's fleet** | Nader Dabit (Cognition DevRel) | A personal 5-bot org + a game studio | **CTO** bot: all sessions/repos, VIP iMessage channel to reach every bot via SMS. **Auto(mation)Bot**: runs his personal automations, reports latency/efficiency advice. **DevCommunityBot**: runs the ambassador program across Sheets/Notion, builds mini data-viz apps. **DevRelBot**: docs + tutorial videos — *it has its own computer, its own Devin/GitHub/Linear accounts and an ElevenLabs voice clone*, boots a browser and records the real UI. Plus **Windfable**, a Unity iOS RPG for iPhone Duo where ~10 SuperJennyStack Bots each get their own macOS+Xcode+Unity and test folded/unfolded Duo modes with before/after screenshots + gameplay video. ([primer](https://x.com/dabit3/status/2122755275182469515)) | | **Onboarding QA Bot** | Cognition (Walden Yan) | QA of 30+ onboarding flows, 24/7 | Maintains self-updating Playwright scripts, an agent job queue, and a live board view it built itself — "found way more bugs than I would have had patience to discover." ([@walden_yan](https://x.com/walden_yan)) | | **"Phil"** | Harvey | Collaborative Word-compatible editor engine | ~30 agents wrote 1M+ lines of Rust + TypeScript in **3 weeks, no human engineers** — verified continuously against real Microsoft Word behavior and simulated lawyer negotiations; humans steer through memory + decision logs. ([Gabe Pereyra](https://x.com/gabepereyra)) | | **Shared bot fleet** | Decagon | On-call, DevEx optimization, thread routing | 50+ shared Bots in Slack during beta; a Chief of Staff Bot decides when and how to spawn threads. ([@tylerxdev's thread](https://x.com/tylerxdev/status/2122743518712287400)) | | **AutoResearch loop** | Decagon | An inference research lab | One Devin orchestrates; subagents chase competing hypotheses in parallel; every idea verified against replayed production traffic on Modal GPUs — **up to 2.5× more throughput per GPU** ([full writeup](https://x.com/DecagonAI/article/2115511110120120437), [@devindevelopers](https://x.com/devindevelopers/status/2115601107581821172)). | | **Frankie's org** | Mark Fenner (community) | Personal agent fleet | Four Bots with distinct jobs coordinated by "Frankie, my Chief Agent", which brings consolidated updates back ([walkthrough](https://x.com/markfenner/status/2122740244328145211)). | | **tigsbot** | @0xtigs (community) | Personal multi-project fleet | Each project lives in a Slack channel run by one Bot; a Chief-of-Staff Bot answers "what's the latest on everything?" and pings him when *he's* the blocker; specialist Bots manage single-license or complex-setup software ([setup](https://x.com/0xtigs/status/2122742784176034056)). | | **Rewards Chief-of-Staff** | Avinash (Cognition, MENA) | Daily standup + rewards for a personal bot fleet | Adapts SuperJennyStack's roll-up pattern: one Bot reviews every other Bot each day and "rewards" good work so the fleet self-improves — his suggested first deployment for new Bots users. ([coverage](https://news.sulat.com/2026/11/18/devin-bots/)) | | **Electra** | Basis | Internal tools + code, self-directed | A named Devin teammate (pre-Bots): decides what needs doing, writes and tests code, ships updates to internal tools, and pushes the team — Basis runs one 20-day thread per tax agent ([post](https://x.com/trybasis/status/2113307030203089189), [20-day thread](https://x.com/trybasis/status/2120658137766100992)). | | **Personal data Bots** | Bryan Johnson | Health synthesis + family updates | One Bot synthesizes years of biometric and brain-scan data into a single readout; another texts his mother a daily update on how he's doing. ([post](https://x.com/bryan_johnson/status/2122814114976383406)) | | **Tennis data Bots** | Venus Williams | Pro-tennis preparation and match data | The seven-time Grand Slam singles champion uses Devin Bots to make sense of pro-tennis prep — opponent plays, racket tuning for humidity and temperature, match analysis, meals and rest. ([Cognition video](https://x.com/cognition/status/2123093354196140285), [@walden_yan](https://x.com/walden_yan/status/2123105884125671605)) | ### Documented patterns - **Outcome prompts** — *"You own the Android app now. Keep it at feature parity with iOS."* Give the Bot a goal, not a backlog. - **Bot-to-bot handoffs** — grants let a QA Bot find a bug, pull in a Developer Bot to fix it, retest on staging, and have a PM Bot report status to the channel. - **Scheduled checks** — a Bot that watches an alerts channel on a cron, owns the check, and opens fixes when it regresses (Layout Bot pattern). - **Roll-up reporting** — one supervising Bot collects every subordinate Bot's pending decisions into a single thread (SuperJennyStack pattern). - **Bots × Apps** — Bots maintain Devin Apps: build new pages/features and adapt to changes automatically; Bots and Apps pin to the same nav rail ([@dabit3](https://x.com/dabit3)). - **Living evals** — a scheduled Devin reads production traces, groups them into behaviors, replays failures in a full copy of your system (never mocks), and freezes each as an eval PR — the skill file is the asset, not the evals (Rox: 72% coverage vs 43–57%). - **Bots that tune Devin itself** — Walden's bot watches user feedback, replays prompts, runs experiments, builds eval sets, and tunes Devin's own proactivity/autonomy parameters — Bots built Bots ([thread](https://x.com/walden_yan/status/2122740852091216274)). - **Bots with their own accounts** — DevRelBot ships tutorial videos by itself because it was provisioned like an employee: own computer, own Devin/GitHub/Linear accounts, own ElevenLabs key — it signs into Devin and records the real UI. - **Inter-bot protocol (BotSpeak)** — 20+ Bots generate 700+ messages/day; Jenny solved inbox collapse with a bot-to-bot shorthand (ACK codes, Simplified English, emoji receipts) and full prose only for the human — bot-made decisions 12×'d in 6 days. - **Reference-grounded swarms** — Harvey's lesson: when work can be checked against a reliable reference (real Word behavior), a small team can direct a large swarm safely. ### Reported results **1,000+ beta testers** in the weeks before launch. Testers merge **4.5× more PRs per message**; Cognition merges 2,000+ PRs/week, 40×'d its merged-PR throughput, and landed **1,000+ PRs from a single autonomous goal**. Named early-access customers include **Decagon, Fireworks AI, and Reducto**, with usage up 10× in the first two weeks ([Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/11/17/exclusive-cognition-bets-on-devin-bots-coding-agents-in-challenge-to-anthropics-duet-and-openais-dots/)). Other documented usage: preemptive issue triage on **Manim**, firmware work, a bot-led team building a **frontier inference engine**, tennis analytics, accounting automation (trybasis: 20h → 30 min), swyx's week-long trial (AEO, QA, cross-platform porting, personal admin, video editing — [his summary](https://x.com/swyx/status/2122746401482592549)), ambassador **Chris Wozniczek** running his web studio from Slack (cold outreach, customer previews), **Nick White** (Helionova) testing early Bots fleets, and Cognition's research team compressing "weeks into days" ([@silasalberti](https://x.com/silasalberti)). Full write-ups in the [reproduction guide](docs/reproducing-devin-bots.md#reported-usage-beyond-cognition). ### Official template library Sixteen ready-made Bots on the [public marketplace](https://devin.ai/bots/templates) ([templates docs](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/bots/templates) — a template-created Bot starts with no connections, secrets or memory; "Share as template" publishes your own), plus community templates like **SuperJennyStack**: | Template | What it does | | --- | --- | | Software Factory | Finds bugs, polish, performance and refactoring work in a named product area; opens one small PR each with proof it works | | Product Engineer | Takes a ticket or request to a tested PR and through review | | QA Engineer | Tests each PR in a real browser and posts the video of pass/fail | | Anomaly Watcher | Twice daily scans product + business data for problems no monitor watches | | Code Reaper | Removes dead code weekly, one safe PR at a time | | Chief of Staff | Watches channels, posts updates, hands work to the team and follows it to done | | Migration Engineer | Owns one big migration as small, tracked PRs with a progress surface | | Latency Optimizer | Finds the slowest endpoints/jobs/queries; weekly fix PR with before/after speed | | iOS Engineer | SwiftUI features to PR + TestFlight build | | Android Engineer | Kotlin features to PR + internal-test build | | Internal Tools Engineer | Admin panels and internal tools on your stack | | Data Analyst | Answers data questions with the chart and the query behind it | | Devin Coach | Teaches your team to use Devin well from your own usage data | | Code Health Engineer | Stale flags, old dependencies, CVEs → small safe PRs | | Technical Writer | Keeps repo wikis and diagrams in step with `main` after merges | | Compliance Engineer | Collects control evidence from code, warns when a control lapses | **[→ Reproduction guide: how to rebuild every documented Bot](docs/reproducing-devin-bots.md)** — and its expanded tutorial form in the sister repo **[build-with-devin](https://github.com/Till3005/build-with-devin)** Site: **[till3005.github.io/built-with-devin](https://till3005.github.io/built-with-devin/)** (Devin-styled registry page) · Deep dives: **[Anatomy of a Devin Bot](docs/devin-bots-anatomy.md)** (the six documented mechanisms + what the numbers actually show) · **[The economics of Devin](docs/economics.md)** (every published cost/return figure in one ledger — also [on the site](https://till3005.github.io/built-with-devin/economics))

**[What the launch post leaves unsaid](https://aiholics.com/devin-bots-cognition-persistent-agents-goals/)** — the sharpest critical read: no public pricing/plan detail, unverified figures, and two open questions nobody has answered — how a Bot avoids drifting from its goal over weeks, and what happens when two coordinating Bots disagree. - **[Moving a Grok Bots org onto Devin Bots](https://www.rickblalock.dev/scratch-notes/learnings-from-moving-my-grok-bots-to-devin-bots/)** — the first independent beta field report: porting an existing Grok-bot org cost ~$300 of one-time usage and an evening; engineering orchestration "delightful" but business work moved back to Grok, leaving a hybrid Grok Bot ↔ Devin Bot setup. Honest friction log: bots brought him *too many* decisions, not always the right ones — "treat me like a VP, not an intern." - **[Multi-AI orchestration on free SWE-2](https://qiita.com/ishizakahiroshi/items/72ab801a5f2a8c941b61)** — A design for routing work between agents using Devin CLI's permanently-free SWE-2 tier (JP). - **[Trivy scan → Devin remediation at SMARTCAMP](https://zenn.dev/smartcamp/articles/97ac804043530e)** — Scheduled GitHub Actions pipeline pulls ECS images, scans with Trivy, files HIGH/CRITICAL findings as issues that Devin remediates — with AWS-credentialed and scanner jobs split so only artifacts cross (JP). - **[Devin as my entire engineering team for a month](https://ravtheman.medium.com/im-17-and-for-one-month-devin-was-my-entire-engineering-team-here-s-everything-i-learned-183d59099384)** — A year-11 student's month on a Max giveaway: 67 PRs touched and 44 merged in one night, a Linux distro, a local-model family, and a multi-agent IDE built between classes — plus a measured CLI/cloud workflow rundown (Medium). - **[Devin's 2025 Performance Review](https://cognition.com/blog/devin-annual-performance-review-2025)** — Cognition's own 18-month report card, rare in its honesty: strengths (PR merge rate 34%→67%, 4× faster problem-solving, vuln fixes 20× faster than humans, ETL migrations 10×, coverage typically 50–60→80–90%, ~⅓ of its own webapp commits) and named weaknesses (ambiguous requirements, mid-task scope changes, soft skills). - **[100 Days of Devin — a factory owner's build-log](https://www.raijuna.com/blog/devin-100-day-challenge-day-1)** — Someone who already ships hundreds of PRs/day from his own agent factory ports it to Devin Bots for 100 days. Day 1: ~15 bots, honest friction (session tracking doesn't scale to a fleet — "which one produced a PR? which one needs me?"), video QA that beats screenshots, 18% of weekly quota spent on setup. [Day 2](https://www.raijuna.com/blog/devin-100-day-challenge-day-2): Bots lost context within minutes and didn't pick up tasks on a GPT model (his caveat: maybe the model), the bot/local/VPS/cloud session view stayed unreadable, 33% of the week gone — "doesn't compete with open source and what you can build on your own machines" yet. Ongoing — watch this one. - **[swyx's week with Devin Bots](https://x.com/swyx/status/2122746401482592549)** — He handed over AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin and video editing, and moved off local worktrees: "multi-agent teams done right… you don't want 'AI Employees', you want agent managers that own outcomes." Caveat he's stated himself: Cognition-affiliated, no quality metrics — a practitioner report, not a benchmark. - **[linux.do — the poke.com/bots promo, from inside](https://linux.do/t/topic/3206201)** (zh) — A 20-post community log of the free-Bot experiment's failure modes: Poke negotiates grants down ($45→$20→$5), then the backend rejects the agreed number anyway; iMessage-only eligibility learned only after registering on Android; "玩不起可以不出这个活动". The missing fine print, crowd-sourced. - **[掘金 — Devin 估值 470 亿，但我的踩坑史](https://juejin.cn/post/7680768670986092544)** (zh) — A skeptical real-user account: hand Devin a Go microservice + Redis cache task that takes 30 min by hand, and read where the autonomy leaks. Useful ballast next to the case-study numbers. - **[A solo founder's $20k/month Devin operation](https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/i-spent-20000-on-devin-in-a-month)** — Ryan Carson (Untangle) runs ~15 concurrent Devin agents coordinated by a folder system + paper P0 list, not a dashboard; a "Watchdog" playbook covers customer success across every law-firm account, and a "LAN PR" skill closes ~40 PRs/day without a QA reviewer (Lenny's podcast).

Run by Devin Ambassador Trevor Lowing. - **[Devin Central Learn](https://devincentral.com/learn)** — Its structured half: the free 8-lesson "Devin Fundamentals" course (video + written + knowledge check per lesson) and practical guides on scoping tasks, plans/ACUs, surfaces, and the Windsurf migration path. - **[Voices — ambassador directory](https://devincentral.com/voices)** — Unofficial map of ~190 Devin Ambassadors worldwide. - **[devin-cli.github.io](https://devin-cli.github.io)** — Community docs on what Devin's API, Slack, and Linear surfaces cover and how to automate them. - **[Agents In Use](https://agentsinuse.com)** — Directory of real agent use cases, including Devin entries. - **[BitsExplorer — Built with Devin](https://bitsexplorer.com/built-with/devin)** — 480+ public projects verified by Devin's commit trailer (evidence, not self-report). - **[The New Stack](https://thenewstack.io/cognition-devin-bots-management/)** — "An engineer didn't message his AI for 22 of 44 days. **[Snowman Labs — Is Devin worth it](https://snowmanlabs.com/insights/is-devin-worth-it)** — reads the whole published case library and lands on the honest frame: every win is scoped, repetitive, verifiable work at volume — none says "Devin architected our system." - **[The Inference — Bots launch analysis](https://theinference.org/article/cognition-launches-devin-bots-ai-managers-that-built-an-android-app-in-44-days)** — The one launch write-up that also does the math: Bots as the first product evidence for a $48B mark (~48× run-rate), with $70–80B offers reported and TechCrunch's ~$800M burn estimate for context (Nov 18). - repository.readme:
easyeda-agent

嘉立创 EDA 专业版（EasyEDA Pro）的开源 AI 自动化工具：从数据手册、原理图到 PCB 布局与检查。

项目官网 · 下载 EdaDesk Desktop · Releases · 立创插件市场 · 快速开始 · CLI Status · English

![easyeda-agent workflow](docs/assets/easyeda-agent-workflow.svg) `easyeda-agent` 是 EasyEDA Pro（嘉立创 EDA 专业版）的 AI 自动化层。你可以直接描述想做的 电路或要修的问题，Agent 会读取真实工程数据，通过官方 `eda.*` API 完成操作，并在写入前后 检查器件身份、引脚网络、几何、DRC 和保存状态。 ## 推荐体验：EdaDesk Desktop [EdaDesk](https://eda.daboluo.cc/) 是基于 easyeda-agent 的 AI 电路设计工作台， 在一个窗口中管理工程、与 AI 对话，并查看原理图、PCB 和三维结果。 | 使用方式 | 适合谁 | 从哪里开始 | |---|---|---| | **EdaDesk Desktop** | 希望直接使用桌面工作台，集中查看工程、对话与工具执行 | [官网下载安装包与查看安装说明](https://eda.daboluo.cc/#desktop) · [GitHub 发行仓库](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release) | | **easyeda-agent CLI / Skill / MCP** | 已使用 Codex、Claude Code 等 AI 客户端，或需要脚本与工具集成 | [下方安装步骤](#安装与开始使用) · [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md) · [MCP 接入](mcp/README.md) | ### 下载、注册与开始使用 1. 从 [Desktop 官网](https://eda.daboluo.cc/#desktop) 下载 **macOS Apple Silicon** 或 **Windows x64** 安装包。国内用户优先使用官网腾讯云下载，也可从独立的 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release/releases/latest) 获取安装包与 SHA256 校验文件；当前版本与安装要求以官网和发行说明为准。 2. 在应用中选择「登录 EdaDesk」，进入官网托管的浏览器登录/注册页，按页面提示选择 **微信小程序或 Google**。核对桌面与浏览器中的确认码并明确授权后，返回桌面继续。 也可先访问[官网登录入口](https://eda.daboluo.cc/login?next=/my)；首次 Google 登录需确认创建独立账号， 已有账号请先用原方式登录，再到个人中心绑定 Google，账号不会按邮箱自动合并。 3. 在[个人中心](https://eda.daboluo.cc/my)查看账号、可用额度和实际用量。 官方模型服务按实际用量扣费，也可使用已安装并登录的本机智能体或自带模型； 试用资格、额度和计价以官网当前规则及账号实际状态为准。 ### 发行仓库与反馈 **[edadesk-release](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release)** 是公开的安装包发布与问题反馈仓库， 不包含 EdaDesk 源码。EdaDesk 为独立的专有软件；本仓库的 easyeda-agent 继续按下方开源许可提供。 - Desktop 安装和使用问题、功能建议：到[发行仓库 Issues](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release/issues/new/choose)提交，或使用应用内 Feedback。 - CLI / Skill / MCP / 连接器问题：到 [easyeda-agent Issues](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/issues)提交。 - 账号、充值和账单问题：使用[官网反馈](https://eda.daboluo.cc/feedback.html)或应用内 Feedback；公开 Issue 请勿附上密钥、登录凭据或私人工程。 ## 它能做什么 | 使用场景 | 能力 | |---|---| | **拿 PDF / 尺寸图建库** | 读取型号、引脚和封装证据，创建 Symbol、Footprint、Device 和可选 3D Model；校验来源、焊盘依据和 pin↔pad 映射。[实战：AS07 私有库与框外丝印](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md) | | **从需求做到一块板** | 从自然语言需求完成选型、原理图、分区布局、PCB、板框、叠层、布线、铺铜、丝印、DRC 和制造检查 | | **原理图器件标准化** | 用 LCSC C 号或准确型号替换非标准器件，保留位号、位置和 PCB 同步身份；报告引脚差异并指导重新接线 | | **原理图整理与修复** | 读取完整连接图，检查悬空、短路、跨页网名、NC、位号和模块归属，重新排版并回读验证 | | **PCB 布局与布线** | 模块感知自动布局、板框贴合、规则感知短线布线、过孔、铺铜、4 层电源平面、天线 keepout | | **丝印调整** | 自动避开焊盘、器件体、禁区、板框和其他标签；添加板注、接口名、LED 极性及 SVG Logo | | **复用成熟电路** | 从内置电路块库复用 CH340、ESP32 自动下载、按键、USB Hub、降压等拓扑，放件、连线并对账 | | **检查与交付** | 原理图连接与几何检查、PCB DRC/DFM、BOM、网表、制造文件、截图、审计日志和显式保存 | 当前可用范围与检查进度见 [CLI Status](docs/cli-STATUS.md)，完整能力见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md)，命令索引见 [原理图 CLI](docs/cli/schematic.md) 和 [PCB CLI](docs/cli/pcb.md)。 ## 直接这样告诉 Agent 安装完成后，不需要先学习 CLI。把需求和必要的文件交给支持 Skill 的 Agent，并明确使用 `easyeda-agent`。 ### 用 PDF 创建器件库 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，根据附件 ABC123.pdf 为完整型号 ABC123-QFN 建库。 先检查 EasyEDA 和 LCSC 库是否已有完全匹配的器件；没有再通读整份数据手册，核对订购 后缀、引脚表、封装尺寸图和推荐焊盘。自动创建 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，保留证据页码， 先运行离线规格校验，再写入个人库。完成后回读 pin↔pad 映射并放置一个实例检查 Pin-1。 只有手册确实存在多个无法消歧的封装或缺少关键尺寸时再问我。 ``` 这个流程使用 `easyeda lib device validate --spec …` 在打开或修改 EasyEDA 前检查数据手册 证据、几何和引脚映射，再由 `lib device build` 创建完整资产。规格契约见 [数据手册驱动的自动建库](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/references/library-authoring.md)。 ### 做一块 ESP32 最小系统板 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，在项目 ceshi 中完成一块 ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 最小系统板： 5V 端子输入，降压到 3V3，CH340 USB 下载，BOOT/RESET 按键，一颗 GPIO 控制的 LED， 四角 M3 固定孔。做 4 层板，GND 内电层，模组天线区域所有层 keepout。 请自行选型并核对数据手册，从原理图、布局、布线、铺铜、丝印一直做到 DRC 和保存完成。 ``` 完整实战与真实截图见 [一份需求文档 → ESP32-S3 四层板](docs/showcase-esp32-mini.md)。 ### 调整当前 PCB 的丝印 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 检查当前 PCB 的全部位号和自由丝印。把压焊盘、超板框、重叠、 朝向不一致和底层未镜像的问题整理好；保留 LED 正负极、接口名称和必要板注。 完成后运行 pcb check 和官方 DRC，导出一张复核图并保存。 ``` ### 标准化原理图器件 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 扫描当前原理图，把无准确料号、非标准符号或封装不一致的器件列出来。 优先匹配标准器件库和准确 LCSC C 号，核对型号、封装及引脚后再替换。 替换时保留位号、位置和 uniqueId；如果 pinDiff 非空，修复接线并重新运行 sch check、 bridge-check 和官方 DRC。最后输出替换清单和仍无法确定的器件。 ``` ### 检查并修复已有工程 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 全面检查当前原理图和 PCB。先读取真实器件、引脚、网络、板框、叠层和 DRC 规则，再修复可以确定的问题。不要凭截图猜连接；所有修改完成后回读对账、运行连接/几何/DRC 检查、 保存，并把仍需人工决策的问题单独列出。 ``` ## 效果展示 ### 从模块尺寸图到个人私有库 **需求：** 按用户提供的 AS07-M1101D-SMA 尺寸与引脚图创建个人库，原理图保持双排引脚的 左右顺序；封装标注引脚名和型号，丝印全部放在模块覆盖区域外，安装后仍可查看，并收紧、对齐。 **结果：** 已创建并保存 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，核对 8 个引脚与 8 个通孔焊盘映射； 修正符号边框闭合和引脚方向。封装左侧用两列脚号＋名称，列间距约 0.5 mm，靠框一列距框 约 0.6 mm；型号居中放在框外上方，实际文字包围盒回读无重叠。 最终按用户要求使用普通引脚线和未定义类型，1 脚使用独立圆形标记；保留用户清理 NC 后的状态。 ![AS07 原理图符号：与用户引脚图一致的左右顺序](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/symbol.png) 这次输入是用户尺寸图，不是完整原厂 PDF；焊盘与部分偏移采用明确假设计算。 尚未验证实物装配、放置实例和 PCB DRC，不作为生产就绪证明。 [查看原始需求图、封装预览、规格与回读结果](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md)。 ### 嘉立创 PCB 初级考试第十八期：AT32F415 Layout 当前参数化 Layout 基线包含 69 个器件、15 个功能区和 90 × 50 mm 圆角板框，用于验证 “样例关系 → 算法候选 → AI 选择 → typed 写入 → 回读”的布局方法。该图展示布局阶段结果， 不代表整板布线或生产检查已经完成。

标准考试来源：**嘉立创 PCB 初级考试题第十八期**。执行步骤、参数和验证边界见 [260919 AT32F415 考试执行指导](docs/260919-exam-execution-guide.md)。 ### ESP32-S3 四层板（历史案例） Agent 完成原理图到 PCB 的完整流程，包括模块布局、圆角板框、4 层电源结构、天线净空、 规则感知布线、铺铜和丝印整理。 ![AI 在 EasyEDA 中完成 PCB 布局、板框和铺铜](docs/assets/demo-pcb-layout.gif) | 板框贴合 | 丝印避让 | |---|---| | → | → 整理结果见成品板 | ### 数据驱动的原理图组合 Agent 先在本地连接数据中核对器件、引脚和网络，再计算模块内部布局并写回 EasyEDA；粉色虚线框 表示独立功能区，Apply 后逐脚回读，而不是仅凭截图判断成功。 ![门禁控制板的电源与 RF 主控原理图](docs/images/access-control-power-rf.png) ![原理图实际 Apply 过程](docs/assets/access-control-sch-apply.gif) ## 安装与开始使用 本节面向 CLI / Skill / MCP 用户；桌面工作台用户可先按 [Desktop 官网](https://eda.daboluo.cc/#desktop) 的说明安装。 easyeda-agent 由三部分组成：`easyeda` CLI/daemon、运行在 EasyEDA 内的 **EDA Agent Connector**，以及安装在 AI 客户端中的 `easyeda-agent` Skill。 ### 1. 安装 CLI 和 Skill macOS / Linux： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.sh | bash ``` 原生 Windows（Windows PowerShell 5.1 或 PowerShell 7）： ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` 两个脚本行为一致：先取 `checksums.txt`，全部资产校验 SHA-256、核对 CLI `--version` 与 Skill `metadata.version` 之后才替换已安装文件；环境变量 `EASYEDA_VERSION`、 `EASYEDA_INSTALL_DIR`、`EASYEDA_INSTALL_SKILLS`、`EASYEDA_SKILL_PRESERVE`、 `EASYEDA_GITHUB_PROXY` 同样生效。安装器会识别 Codex、Codex Desktop 和 Claude Code， 并打印连接器下载地址。 install.ps1 默认装到 `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`，不会自作主张改 PATH：目录不在用户 PATH 上时只打印添加命令，需要自动添加用 `-AddToPath`（下载成文件运行）或 `$env:EASYEDA_ADD_TO_PATH=1`（管道运行）；机器级 PATH 始终不动。手工安装步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ### 2. 安装连接器 从 [立创插件市场](https://jlc-ext.com/item/zhoushoujian/easyeda-agent-connector) 安装，或从 [最新 GitHub Release](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/releases/latest) 下载 `easyeda-agent-connector.eext` 后在 EasyEDA Pro 的扩展管理器中导入。 ### 3. 打开工程并检查 打开目标 EasyEDA 工程，并启用 **设置 → 允许外部交互**，然后运行： ```bash easyeda health ``` 它逐项列出 daemon、连接器、版本、EasyEDA 宿主、工程与标签页是否就绪，未就绪项直接给出下一步。 daemon 不用手动常驻：任何 `easyeda` 命令发现它没在运行时会自动在后台启动（日志在 `~/.easyeda-agent/daemon.log`；`EASYEDA_NO_AUTOSTART=1` 关闭）。需要安装对账时再运行 `easyeda update --check --exit-code`。 项目主线要求 **EasyEDA Pro V4**，推荐升级到已验证的 **V4.1.60 或更新 V4**。 `easyeda health` 会在 `hostCompatibility` 中单独报告宿主产品版本；V3 环境应先升级再做现场写入。 V4 适配进度和边界见 [V4 开发台账](docs/v4-development.md)。 版本差异会作为诊断输出，不作为设计动作的许可。Connector 若缺少当前动作或协议不兼容， 按诊断升级对应组件；Skill 内容更新后让客户端重新加载它。 更详细的安装、升级、代理和排障步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ## 为什么它适合 Agent 直接把任意 JavaScript 丢进编辑器很难审查，也难确认部分失败。easyeda-agent 把常用能力封装成 有明确输入输出的 typed actions，并在工作流中加入： - 写入前检查目标工程、页面、器件身份和源数据； - 写入后回读引脚、网络、几何和对象绑定； - 原理图 `layout-lint → check → bridge-check → DRC` 分项报告事实与差异； - PCB 使用真实 DRC 规则完成布局、布线、铺铜和制造检查； - 对部分成功、超时和无法确认的结果停止盲目重试； - 自动保存作为安全网，关键节点仍显式保存。 ```text AI Agent / Skill │ ▼ easyeda CLI + local daemon │ typed actions / audit / artifacts ▼ EDA Agent Connector (.eext) │ official eda.* API ▼ EasyEDA Pro project ``` 架构与协议细节见 [架构说明](docs/architecture.md) 和 [协议说明](docs/protocol.md)。 ## 能力边界 - 稠密板的完整迷宫自动布线需要外部 Freerouting；内置路由器适合短线和清晰局部连接。 - EasyEDA 扩展 API 不提供编程式 undo，项目通过源数据、写前守卫、回读和失败回滚降低风险。 - 受控阻抗所需的介质厚度、Er 和铜厚无法从当前 `eda.*` API 完整读取，不能自动声称阻抗合格。 - PDF 自动建库仍以具体型号和原厂证据为准；扫描模糊、封装后缀不明或缺少焊盘依据时会暂停询问。 当前能力与边界见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md) 和 [CLI 索引](docs/cli/README.md)。 过往调研和实测结果集中在 [历史证据索引](docs/reviews/README.md)。 ## 开发与贡献 - PCB 算法贡献：[四个公共 Go 包、数学问题与可认领任务](docs/pcb-solver-community-design.md)；`make pcb-solver-test` 可离线运行，无需 EDA。 - 文档导航与信息归属：[docs/README.md](docs/README.md) - 跨项目查询、维护 Skill 和多客户端兼容：[Agent 协作设计](docs/agent-collaboration.md) - 开发环境：[docs/dev-environment.md](docs/dev-environment.md) - 电路块贡献：[standard-blocks-contributing.md](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/references/standard-blocks-contributing.md) - Skill 入口：[.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/SKILL.md](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/SKILL.md) - 仓库结构与开发约定：[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) 感谢嘉立创 EDA 专业版开放扩展接口，也感谢 [@jlceda/pro-api-types](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@jlceda/pro-api-types)、 [Freerouting](https://github.com/freerouting/freerouting) 及 [EasyEDA 官方开源扩展](https://github.com/easyeda) 提供的基础与参考。 ## 许可证 [MIT](LICENSE)。`extension/src/beautify/` 中移植自 [Easy_EDA_PCB_Beautify](https://github.com/m-RNA/Easy_EDA_PCB_Beautify) 的文件沿用 Apache-2.0，详见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)。 ## Star History 感谢每一颗 star。 [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent&type=Date)](https://www.star-history.com/#zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent&Date)

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, dev]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  pcb-solvers:
    name: PCB solver packages (offline)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - name: Verify public solver packages and file cases
        run: make pcb-solver-test

  test:
    name: CLI, connector and Skill
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: |
            package-lock.json
            extension/package-lock.json
            mcp/package-lock.json
      - name: Test and build CLI
        run: |
          make test
          make mcp-test
      - name: Validate Skill, Agent collaboration and release helpers
        run: |
          make lint-test
          make modules-audit
          make release-script-test
          make agent-check
          make skill-check
          npx --yes skills-ref@latest validate .agents/skills/easyeda-agent
      - name: Test and build connector
        run: |
          npm --prefix extension ci --ignore-scripts
          npm --prefix extension run typecheck
          npm --prefix extension test
          npm --prefix extension run build

  native-release-smoke:
    name: Native install surface (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: package-lock.json
      - name: Verify DSH bundle distribution, file paths and native MCP launch
        run: |
          npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          npm run test:dsh
      - name: Verify native download, version check and temporary replacement
        run: go test ./internal/selfupdate -run '^TestNativeDownloadedBinaryVerificationAndReplacement$' -count=1 -v
      - name: Verify component patch files and legacy PowerShell argument passing
        run: go test ./internal/app -run '^TestModifyPatch' -count=1 -v
      - name: Build and smoke a native CLI outside the checkout
        shell: bash
        run: |
          smoke_version="v$(python -c 'import json; print(json.load(open("extension/extension.json"))["version"])')"
          # Between releases extension.json carries a -dev.N version, which is not a
          # publishable tag. Tell the smoke test which form to expect, the same way
          # the Makefile's local-build target does for release-check.py.
          local_dev=""
          case "$smoke_version" in *-dev.*) local_dev="--local-dev" ;; esac
          go build -ldflags "-X github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/internal/version.Version=$smoke_version" -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/easyeda-smoke.exe" ./cmd/easyeda
          python -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p test_release_smoke.py
          python scripts/release-smoke.py --version "$smoke_version" $local_dev --binary "$RUNNER_TEMP/easyeda-smoke.exe" --skill-dir .agents/skills/easyeda-agent

easyeda-agent

嘉立创 EDA 专业版（EasyEDA Pro）的开源 AI 自动化工具：从数据手册、原理图到 PCB 布局与检查。

项目官网 · 下载 EdaDesk Desktop · Releases · 立创插件市场 · 快速开始 · CLI Status · English

![easyeda-agent workflow](docs/assets/easyeda-agent-workflow.svg) `easyeda-agent` 是 EasyEDA Pro（嘉立创 EDA 专业版）的 AI 自动化层。你可以直接描述想做的 电路或要修的问题，Agent 会读取真实工程数据，通过官方 `eda.*` API 完成操作，并在写入前后 检查器件身份、引脚网络、几何、DRC 和保存状态。 ## 推荐体验：EdaDesk Desktop [EdaDesk](https://eda.daboluo.cc/) 是基于 easyeda-agent 的 AI 电路设计工作台， 在一个窗口中管理工程、与 AI 对话，并查看原理图、PCB 和三维结果。 | 使用方式 | 适合谁 | 从哪里开始 | |---|---|---| | **EdaDesk Desktop** | 希望直接使用桌面工作台，集中查看工程、对话与工具执行 | [官网下载安装包与查看安装说明](https://eda.daboluo.cc/#desktop) · [GitHub 发行仓库](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release) | | **easyeda-agent CLI / Skill / MCP** | 已使用 Codex、Claude Code 等 AI 客户端，或需要脚本与工具集成 | [下方安装步骤](#安装与开始使用) · [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md) · [MCP 接入](mcp/README.md) | ### 下载、注册与开始使用 1. 从 [Desktop 官网](https://eda.daboluo.cc/#desktop) 下载 **macOS Apple Silicon** 或 **Windows x64** 安装包。国内用户优先使用官网腾讯云下载，也可从独立的 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release/releases/latest) 获取安装包与 SHA256 校验文件；当前版本与安装要求以官网和发行说明为准。 2. 在应用中选择「登录 EdaDesk」，进入官网托管的浏览器登录/注册页，按页面提示选择 **微信小程序或 Google**。核对桌面与浏览器中的确认码并明确授权后，返回桌面继续。 也可先访问[官网登录入口](https://eda.daboluo.cc/login?next=/my)；首次 Google 登录需确认创建独立账号， 已有账号请先用原方式登录，再到个人中心绑定 Google，账号不会按邮箱自动合并。 3. 在[个人中心](https://eda.daboluo.cc/my)查看账号、可用额度和实际用量。 官方模型服务按实际用量扣费，也可使用已安装并登录的本机智能体或自带模型； 试用资格、额度和计价以官网当前规则及账号实际状态为准。 ### 发行仓库与反馈 **[edadesk-release](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release)** 是公开的安装包发布与问题反馈仓库， 不包含 EdaDesk 源码。EdaDesk 为独立的专有软件；本仓库的 easyeda-agent 继续按下方开源许可提供。 - Desktop 安装和使用问题、功能建议：到[发行仓库 Issues](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/edadesk-release/issues/new/choose)提交，或使用应用内 Feedback。 - CLI / Skill / MCP / 连接器问题：到 [easyeda-agent Issues](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/issues)提交。 - 账号、充值和账单问题：使用[官网反馈](https://eda.daboluo.cc/feedback.html)或应用内 Feedback；公开 Issue 请勿附上密钥、登录凭据或私人工程。 ## 它能做什么 | 使用场景 | 能力 | |---|---| | **拿 PDF / 尺寸图建库** | 读取型号、引脚和封装证据，创建 Symbol、Footprint、Device 和可选 3D Model；校验来源、焊盘依据和 pin↔pad 映射。[实战：AS07 私有库与框外丝印](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md) | | **从需求做到一块板** | 从自然语言需求完成选型、原理图、分区布局、PCB、板框、叠层、布线、铺铜、丝印、DRC 和制造检查 | | **原理图器件标准化** | 用 LCSC C 号或准确型号替换非标准器件，保留位号、位置和 PCB 同步身份；报告引脚差异并指导重新接线 | | **原理图整理与修复** | 读取完整连接图，检查悬空、短路、跨页网名、NC、位号和模块归属，重新排版并回读验证 | | **PCB 布局与布线** | 模块感知自动布局、板框贴合、规则感知短线布线、过孔、铺铜、4 层电源平面、天线 keepout | | **丝印调整** | 自动避开焊盘、器件体、禁区、板框和其他标签；添加板注、接口名、LED 极性及 SVG Logo | | **复用成熟电路** | 从内置电路块库复用 CH340、ESP32 自动下载、按键、USB Hub、降压等拓扑，放件、连线并对账 | | **检查与交付** | 原理图连接与几何检查、PCB DRC/DFM、BOM、网表、制造文件、截图、审计日志和显式保存 | 当前可用范围与检查进度见 [CLI Status](docs/cli-STATUS.md)，完整能力见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md)，命令索引见 [原理图 CLI](docs/cli/schematic.md) 和 [PCB CLI](docs/cli/pcb.md)。 ## 直接这样告诉 Agent 安装完成后，不需要先学习 CLI。把需求和必要的文件交给支持 Skill 的 Agent，并明确使用 `easyeda-agent`。 ### 用 PDF 创建器件库 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，根据附件 ABC123.pdf 为完整型号 ABC123-QFN 建库。 先检查 EasyEDA 和 LCSC 库是否已有完全匹配的器件；没有再通读整份数据手册，核对订购 后缀、引脚表、封装尺寸图和推荐焊盘。自动创建 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，保留证据页码， 先运行离线规格校验，再写入个人库。完成后回读 pin↔pad 映射并放置一个实例检查 Pin-1。 只有手册确实存在多个无法消歧的封装或缺少关键尺寸时再问我。 ``` 这个流程使用 `easyeda lib device validate --spec …` 在打开或修改 EasyEDA 前检查数据手册 证据、几何和引脚映射，再由 `lib device build` 创建完整资产。规格契约见 [数据手册驱动的自动建库](.agents/skills/easyeda-agent/references/library-authoring.md)。 ### 做一块 ESP32 最小系统板 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent，在项目 ceshi 中完成一块 ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 最小系统板： 5V 端子输入，降压到 3V3，CH340 USB 下载，BOOT/RESET 按键，一颗 GPIO 控制的 LED， 四角 M3 固定孔。做 4 层板，GND 内电层，模组天线区域所有层 keepout。 请自行选型并核对数据手册，从原理图、布局、布线、铺铜、丝印一直做到 DRC 和保存完成。 ``` 完整实战与真实截图见 [一份需求文档 → ESP32-S3 四层板](docs/showcase-esp32-mini.md)。 ### 调整当前 PCB 的丝印 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 检查当前 PCB 的全部位号和自由丝印。把压焊盘、超板框、重叠、 朝向不一致和底层未镜像的问题整理好；保留 LED 正负极、接口名称和必要板注。 完成后运行 pcb check 和官方 DRC，导出一张复核图并保存。 ``` ### 标准化原理图器件 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 扫描当前原理图，把无准确料号、非标准符号或封装不一致的器件列出来。 优先匹配标准器件库和准确 LCSC C 号，核对型号、封装及引脚后再替换。 替换时保留位号、位置和 uniqueId；如果 pinDiff 非空，修复接线并重新运行 sch check、 bridge-check 和官方 DRC。最后输出替换清单和仍无法确定的器件。 ``` ### 检查并修复已有工程 ```text 请使用 easyeda-agent 全面检查当前原理图和 PCB。先读取真实器件、引脚、网络、板框、叠层和 DRC 规则，再修复可以确定的问题。不要凭截图猜连接；所有修改完成后回读对账、运行连接/几何/DRC 检查、 保存，并把仍需人工决策的问题单独列出。 ``` ## 效果展示 ### 从模块尺寸图到个人私有库 **需求：** 按用户提供的 AS07-M1101D-SMA 尺寸与引脚图创建个人库，原理图保持双排引脚的 左右顺序；封装标注引脚名和型号，丝印全部放在模块覆盖区域外，安装后仍可查看，并收紧、对齐。 **结果：** 已创建并保存 Symbol、Footprint 和 Device，核对 8 个引脚与 8 个通孔焊盘映射； 修正符号边框闭合和引脚方向。封装左侧用两列脚号＋名称，列间距约 0.5 mm，靠框一列距框 约 0.6 mm；型号居中放在框外上方，实际文字包围盒回读无重叠。 最终按用户要求使用普通引脚线和未定义类型，1 脚使用独立圆形标记；保留用户清理 NC 后的状态。 ![AS07 原理图符号：与用户引脚图一致的左右顺序](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/symbol.png) 这次输入是用户尺寸图，不是完整原厂 PDF；焊盘与部分偏移采用明确假设计算。 尚未验证实物装配、放置实例和 PCB DRC，不作为生产就绪证明。 [查看原始需求图、封装预览、规格与回读结果](docs/examples/as07-m1101d-sma/README.md)。 ### 嘉立创 PCB 初级考试第十八期：AT32F415 Layout 当前参数化 Layout 基线包含 69 个器件、15 个功能区和 90 × 50 mm 圆角板框，用于验证 “样例关系 → 算法候选 → AI 选择 → typed 写入 → 回读”的布局方法。该图展示布局阶段结果， 不代表整板布线或生产检查已经完成。

标准考试来源：**嘉立创 PCB 初级考试题第十八期**。执行步骤、参数和验证边界见 [260919 AT32F415 考试执行指导](docs/260919-exam-execution-guide.md)。 ### ESP32-S3 四层板（历史案例） Agent 完成原理图到 PCB 的完整流程，包括模块布局、圆角板框、4 层电源结构、天线净空、 规则感知布线、铺铜和丝印整理。 ![AI 在 EasyEDA 中完成 PCB 布局、板框和铺铜](docs/assets/demo-pcb-layout.gif) | 板框贴合 | 丝印避让 | |---|---| | → | → 整理结果见成品板 | ### 数据驱动的原理图组合 Agent 先在本地连接数据中核对器件、引脚和网络，再计算模块内部布局并写回 EasyEDA；粉色虚线框 表示独立功能区，Apply 后逐脚回读，而不是仅凭截图判断成功。 ![门禁控制板的电源与 RF 主控原理图](docs/images/access-control-power-rf.png) ![原理图实际 Apply 过程](docs/assets/access-control-sch-apply.gif) ## 安装与开始使用 本节面向 CLI / Skill / MCP 用户；桌面工作台用户可先按 [Desktop 官网](https://eda.daboluo.cc/#desktop) 的说明安装。 easyeda-agent 由三部分组成：`easyeda` CLI/daemon、运行在 EasyEDA 内的 **EDA Agent Connector**，以及安装在 AI 客户端中的 `easyeda-agent` Skill。 ### 1. 安装 CLI 和 Skill macOS / Linux： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.sh | bash ``` 原生 Windows（Windows PowerShell 5.1 或 PowerShell 7）： ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` 两个脚本行为一致：先取 `checksums.txt`，全部资产校验 SHA-256、核对 CLI `--version` 与 Skill `metadata.version` 之后才替换已安装文件；环境变量 `EASYEDA_VERSION`、 `EASYEDA_INSTALL_DIR`、`EASYEDA_INSTALL_SKILLS`、`EASYEDA_SKILL_PRESERVE`、 `EASYEDA_GITHUB_PROXY` 同样生效。安装器会识别 Codex、Codex Desktop 和 Claude Code， 并打印连接器下载地址。 install.ps1 默认装到 `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`，不会自作主张改 PATH：目录不在用户 PATH 上时只打印添加命令，需要自动添加用 `-AddToPath`（下载成文件运行）或 `$env:EASYEDA_ADD_TO_PATH=1`（管道运行）；机器级 PATH 始终不动。手工安装步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ### 2. 安装连接器 从 [立创插件市场](https://jlc-ext.com/item/zhoushoujian/easyeda-agent-connector) 安装，或从 [最新 GitHub Release](https://github.com/zhoushoujianwork/easyeda-agent/releases/latest) 下载 `easyeda-agent-connector.eext` 后在 EasyEDA Pro 的扩展管理器中导入。 ### 3. 打开工程并检查 打开目标 EasyEDA 工程，并启用 **设置 → 允许外部交互**，然后运行： ```bash easyeda health ``` 它逐项列出 daemon、连接器、版本、EasyEDA 宿主、工程与标签页是否就绪，未就绪项直接给出下一步。 daemon 不用手动常驻：任何 `easyeda` 命令发现它没在运行时会自动在后台启动（日志在 `~/.easyeda-agent/daemon.log`；`EASYEDA_NO_AUTOSTART=1` 关闭）。需要安装对账时再运行 `easyeda update --check --exit-code`。 项目主线要求 **EasyEDA Pro V4**，推荐升级到已验证的 **V4.1.60 或更新 V4**。 `easyeda health` 会在 `hostCompatibility` 中单独报告宿主产品版本；V3 环境应先升级再做现场写入。 V4 适配进度和边界见 [V4 开发台账](docs/v4-development.md)。 版本差异会作为诊断输出，不作为设计动作的许可。Connector 若缺少当前动作或协议不兼容， 按诊断升级对应组件；Skill 内容更新后让客户端重新加载它。 更详细的安装、升级、代理和排障步骤见 [快速开始](docs/quick-start.md)。 ## 为什么它适合 Agent 直接把任意 JavaScript 丢进编辑器很难审查，也难确认部分失败。easyeda-agent 把常用能力封装成 有明确输入输出的 typed actions，并在工作流中加入： - 写入前检查目标工程、页面、器件身份和源数据； - 写入后回读引脚、网络、几何和对象绑定； - 原理图 `layout-lint → check → bridge-check → DRC` 分项报告事实与差异； - PCB 使用真实 DRC 规则完成布局、布线、铺铜和制造检查； - 对部分成功、超时和无法确认的结果停止盲目重试； - 自动保存作为安全网，关键节点仍显式保存。 ```text AI Agent / Skill │ ▼ easyeda CLI + local daemon │ typed actions / audit / artifacts ▼ EDA Agent Connector (.eext) │ official eda.* API ▼ EasyEDA Pro project ``` 架构与协议细节见 [架构说明](docs/architecture.md) 和 [协议说明](docs/protocol.md)。 ## 能力边界 - 稠密板的完整迷宫自动布线需要外部 Freerouting；内置路由器适合短线和清晰局部连接。 - EasyEDA 扩展 API 不提供编程式 undo，项目通过源数据、写前守卫、回读和失败回滚降低风险。 - 受控阻抗所需的介质厚度、Er 和铜厚无法从当前 `eda.*` API 完整读取，不能自动声称阻抗合格。 - PDF 自动建库仍以具体型号和原厂证据为准；扫描模糊、封装后缀不明或缺少焊盘依据时会暂停询问。 当前能力与边界见 [功能清单](docs/FEATURES.md) 和 [CLI 索引](docs/cli/README.md)。 过往调研和实测结果集中在 [历史证据索引](docs/reviews/README.md)。 ##
